Reform UK says it has suspended members of the party after an undercover ITV investigation secretly filmed councillors and election candidates calling Muslims “parasites” and describing Black children as “animals”.

One even called for King Charles to be beheaded, arguing it was because he “is a Muslim”.

The footage, part of a documentary by ITV Exposure to be screened on Sunday night, followed Reform UK candidates and councillors across England and Wales during the May local elections and four by-election campaigns in 2025 and 2026.

It recorded a senior Reform councillor in Solihull saying of Asian people: “Drag them out of their homes, stick them on planes and f*** them off to Pakistan.”

Speaking about a female Reform candidate, another Reform male councillor from the town said “if she was my daughter, it would still be bath night on a Thursday”.

In response, Reform UK accused ITV of “extreme methods of deception” during the undercover investigation.

open image in gallery Alan Feeney, who is no longer a Reform UK councillor, was filmed saying his area had been ‘infested’ with Asian families ( ITV )

The party said: "Not all individuals covertly recorded by ITV are members of Reform UK. Where members, activists and councillors have clearly behaved inappropriately, investigations have commenced. In some cases, there have been suspensions and due process must be followed.”

Reform UK also said it had improved its vetting procedures “but from time to time, a handful of individuals who do not share our values will initially make it through vetting. This is the same for all organisations.”

It added: “There is no room for racism in Reform UK."

The investigation came “at a time when Nigel Farage and other members of Reform are being targeted by individuals who wished them harm and caused a security issue which was documented during the course of the undercover investigation”, but was not included in the report, the party said.

In September 2024, Nigel Farage promised he would improve the party’s vetting process saying “we don't want extremists, we don't want bigots, we don’t want people who think that way, because we represent the silent, decent majority of this great country that we live in.”

The documentary recorded Reform Councillor Alan Feeney in Solihull saying the area had been “infested” with Asian families, and called them “absolute parasites”.

open image in gallery Dean Miller said he would ‘take them out’ when referring to illegal immigrants crossing the Channel ( ITV )

Speaking about Muslims, he said “they're in our judiciary, they're in our schools, they're in our healthcare, they're everywhere, and they are not working on our side, they're against us".

He also said he believed that “no more than one percent of British population can be non-white”.

He added: “You almost need to out-Muslim the Muslims.

“You'd need a proper nuclear option, like literally drag them at their homes, stick them on planes and f*** them off to Pakistan. Which you’ll never do in a month of Sundays….You just have to make it a country they don’t want to be in… I mean you’re getting to a point where you ban Muslims from standing from public office”.

Another election candidate in Solihull, Chris Whelan, said of a female Reform candidate: “If she was my daughter, it would still be bath night on a Thursday. I'll wash you properly this time.”

ITV reported that on Monday evening Councillor Feeney said he had "mutually agreed” to resign from Reform UK, citing “personal reasons”, and would be continuing as an Independent councillor and that Councillor Whelan had also resigned from Reform for personal and health reasons.

The Independent has approached both men.

open image in gallery In September 2024, Nigel Farage promised he would improve the party’s vetting process ( House of Commons )

Dean Miller, a Reform councillor for Bromley, said of illegal immigrants crossing the Channel: “I’d get nicked for saying what I would do. Do you know what I mean? I’ll take them out bruv, I don’t care… the way I see it, you’ve got to kill or you’re going to be killed... These f*ckers have come to rape and pillage and f*cking kill us. There's no doubt about it.”

He was filmed undercover calling for King Charles to be beheaded: "Apparently King Charles is a f*cking Muslim… someone from the inside saw a f*cking prayer mat and all that in one of his f*cking rooms … I think that’s f*cking traitorous“.

ITV said he later told the programme he is disabled and was heavily medicated at the time, and has resigned from Reform. The Independent has approached Councillor Miller.

In Makerfield, Raymond Dunning, a Reform councillor in Tameside, Greater Manchester, said he would have “18 to 30-year-old young lads, train them up in the army in insurgency tactics so they can go street by street, house by house, picking the c**ts up.” The Independent has approached Councillor Dunning.

Labour chair Bridget Phillipson said: “The extreme racism and appalling behaviour exposed by this investigation is truly sickening. Nigel Farage can’t shrug these latest revelations off as being a few bad apples. Every Reform councillor, council candidate or party member found to have made such despicable comments must be thrown out of Reform UK immediately.

“Nigel Farage needs to explain why this keeps happening in his party and why he is failing to deal with blatant racism among those who stand for public office with his backing. It’s clear that Farage and his party are determined to poison our politics and threaten the shared British values Labour will always proudly defend.@

Liberal Democrat leader Sir Ed Davey described the report as “chilling”, and said: “I feel for anyone watching this tonight who is frightened to see such racism and hatred festering in their community.”

A Conservative Party spokesman said: “Nigel Farage promised to make Reform ready for government. These sorry individuals are proof he has failed.”

Undercover: A Year In Reform will be aired on Sunday 18th October at 10.20pm on ITV1, ITVX, STV & STV Player

News.title: House Republicans are secretly admitting that they will lose the majority in November: report
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Some Republicans in the House of Representatives have secretly admitted that they will lose the majority in the midterm elections this November, according to a new report.

President Donald Trump has been fiercely campaigning for GOP candidates in red states that would normally be easy for Republicans to win. Trump has recently held rallies in Texas, Ohio and Alaska to stump for Republican Senate candidates, but members of his party are reportedly worried that the House will slip through their fingers.

Five senior Republicans on Capitol Hill anonymously aired their concerns to Politico, with one saying that the party just hopes to “save as many Republican seats as we can.”

“President Trump has made this election all about himself,” the House Republican said. “Now we have to survive that political storm.”

White House Assistant Press Secretary Liz Huston told The Independent, “President Trump is committed to maintaining Republican majorities in both the House and Senate.”

open image in gallery Some Republicans in the House of Representatives have secretly admitted that they will lose the majority in the midterm elections this November, according to a new report ( AFP via Getty Images )

Term-limited Trump has been traveling across the U.S. to plead with his supporters to vote Republican.

“I want you to do me one big favor — pretend that I'm on the ballot because here's what happens. Every time I’ve been on the ballot, we win,” the president said at his rally in Wasilla, Alaska, on Tuesday.

But the president is struggling with record-low approval ratings amid an unpopular Iran war and a high cost of living.

Sixty-five percent of Americans disapproved of Trump’s job as president, while just 32 percent approved in a recent Reuters/Ipsos poll.

Trump has even resorted to promising Americans $5,000 checks if Republicans keep control of Congress, which critics have called a bribe.

“If Republicans win the House of Representatives and the Senate, I’m going to give all adult citizens in the United States $5,000,” the president said in Alaska.

open image in gallery Five senior Republicans on Capitol Hill reportedly aired their concerns, with one saying that the party just hopes to 'save as many Republican seats as we can' ( AFP via Getty Images )

Despite Trump’s best efforts, some congressional Republicans are convinced they won’t be able to pull off a big enough win.

The Congressional Leadership Fund, the leading super PAC supporting House Republican candidates, canceled advertising in Nebraska and Iowa to put the money toward other races, Politico reported. The Senate Leadership Fund, the main super PAC backing GOP Senate candidates, then reportedly took the airtime to support Republicans running for Senate seats in those states.

“These are not the moves of a party that’s going to keep the House,” another Republican lawmaker told Politico.

The Congressional Leadership Fund told the outlet it was unwavering in its fight to keep control of the House.

The super PAC’s president, Chris Winkelman, said the goal is to “keep the pressure on the most vulnerable Democrats and preserve a path to 218 seats.”

open image in gallery Term-limited Trump has been traveling across the U.S. to plead with his supporters to vote Republican, telling them to ‘pretend that I'm on the ballot’ ( AFP via Getty Images )

Trump was in Bullhead City, Arizona, Wednesday to campaign for Congressman Andy Biggs, who is running against Democratic incumbent Katie Hobbs for governor, and congressional candidates Mark Lamb and Abe Hamadeh.

At the rally, Trump called Hobbs “dumb” and contrasted her intelligence with that of his on-and-off friend, tech billionaire Elon Musk.

“I know smart people. I deal from Elon [Musk] down to Katie [Hobbs],” Trump said. “Elon’s 80 percent super genius — and 20 percent he got a little problem, I always tell him. He’s a great guy, though.”

He told the crowd, “We gotta elect” Biggs. “I'm here to help him and some of your great congressmen,” the president said.

News.title: Oregon father of five killed in home by suspected stray bullet shot by hunter
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

An Oregon father of five was fatally shot inside his home on Saturday by a stray bullet that police suspect was fired by a hunter.

Robert Alan Church, 54, died at his residence in the 24000 block of Springer Road near Sweet Home, Oregon, the Linn County Sheriff’s Office said in a news release.

Emergency personnel from the sheriff’s office and Sweet Home Fire Department responded to a report of a shooting around 5:48 p.m. and attempted lifesaving measures, but Church died at the scene.

Investigators determined that the shot likely originated from a hunter in the vicinity who partially field dressed a deer before leaving the area with the carcass.

Linn County Sheriff Michelle Duncan said that investigators did not know whether the hunter was aware that Church had been hit, as reported by FOX 12 Oregon. Duncan added that officials did not believe the discharge was intentional and urged the person responsible to come forward to bring closure to the victim’s family.

open image in gallery Robert Alan Church, 54, died at his Sweet Home, Oregon, residence after a bullet fired by a hunter entered his home on Saturday ( Bob Church/Facebook )

Residents in the neighborhood observed that the surrounding rural area is a frequent destination for hunting, calling on hunters to exercise caution regarding their surroundings and target backstops, according to FOX 12 Oregon.

Church is survived by five children. His daughter Shy remembered her father as “one of a kind” and said that he “loved his children more than anything in the world,” the local station reported.

In an online GoFundMe campaign titled “Easing the Burden for Robert’s Family,” Shy described the emotional and financial strain following the incident.

“His death was sudden, shocking, and impossible for our family to prepare for,” she wrote. “Robert's life was taken because someone who was hunting was not mindful and shot toward a home.”

Shyanne wrote that Church’s father was raising two foster children and covering cremation expenses, but could not manage the surrounding costs.

“My grandpa is covering Robert’s cremation, but he cannot afford the many other costs that come with losing someone so suddenly,” she wrote.

The campaign has collected $2,412, surpassing its $1,000 target. Money from the fundraiser will cover moving and storage fees for Church’s belongings, travel costs for relatives, memorial expenses and food for the family.

Detectives are asking anyone who was present on Springer Road on the evening of October 10 to contact the sheriff’s office. Investigators are specifically seeking details on parked vehicles, people observed with a deer, audio of gunshots, or any home surveillance or trail camera recordings.

Anyone with information is asked to contact Linn County Sheriff’s Office Detective Derek Klein at 541-967-3950.

News.title: Trump team under fire for delaying IRS report on the impact of his tax cuts: ‘I think they’re hiding stuff’
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Donald Trump’s administration appears to be withholding critical data that is expected to show the sweeping impacts of the president’s massive domestic spending bill that analysts say has increased taxes and household costs for Americans from virtually every economic background.

IRS data is typically released after each filing season, but the administration has delayed the publication of this year’s report that would provide the first detailed look into the impacts of Trump’s One Big Beautiful Bill Act — and may reveal the agency’s failures to audit wealthy households.

The report is currently listed on the IRS website as “pending.” That data was supposed to be published in July and updated in September. Neither has happened, and the IRS is waiting for the Treasury Department to sign off on the release, according to Politico.

Those details could be embarrassing for congressional Republicans while the White House tries to convince voters in the days before midterm elections that his signature piece of legislation was a success — with the balance of power in Congress and fate of Trump’s final two years in office at stake.

“I think they are hiding stuff that doesn’t line up with all the crowing the CEO has been doing,” Center for Taxpayer Rights executive director Nina Olsen told Politico about Trump’s IRS chief Frank Bisignano.

open image in gallery Missing IRS reports under chief Frank Bisignano could be embarrassing to congressional Republicans running on Trump’s message of economic success, experts say ( AFP/Getty )

A recent analysis from the Institute on Taxation and Economic Policy determined that the One Big Beautiful Bill “overwhelmingly benefits the rich and corporations.”

Alleged benefits to middle-class households, including the president’s “no tax on tips” mantra, represent only “a very small portion of the overall legislation which overwhelmingly benefits high-income people and corporations,” according to the report.

Massive corporations including Meta, Amazon, Google and Tesla “have paid extremely low effective tax rates” — from 0 percent to 8 percent — “in large part” due to Trump’s bill, the report found.

The president’s chief economic policy has largely hiked taxes and consumer costs for low- and middle-income households while cutting them for the top 1 percent, according to the report, which was published October 8.

“The tax cuts Americans were promised — which were tilted heavily to the top to start — are being overwhelmed by higher prices and higher health care costs for most families,” according to Steve Wamhoff, the group’s federal policy director and the author of the report.

“When you look at the full picture rather than tax cuts in isolation, the result is striking: the typical American in every income group is paying more, except that the richest 1 percent is the one group that comes out ahead,” he said.

open image in gallery The IRS has already come under fire for missing data about the ‘tax cap’ that should shot how much tax goes uncollected after the Treasury Department’s inspector general found that audits plunged by more than a third ( AFP/Getty )

The IRS has already come under fire for withholding the report’s estimate of unpaid taxes, an estimate of the so-called “tax gap” that reveals how much tax goes uncollected each year.

The agency’s most recent projection estimated that roughly $700 billion in owed taxes went uncollected in 2022. The estimate for 2023 was never released, let alone the reports for 2024, 2025 and 2026.

This summer, the Treasury Department’s inspector general found that revenue collected from audits dropped by more than a third over the last fiscal year, suggesting that the tax gap is likely growing under Trump.

That drop coincided with a 27 percent cut in enforcement and collection staffing at the IRS under Elon Musk’s so-called Department of Government Efficiency.

“The downstream effects of these reductions are likely to become more apparent over time,” the inspector general wrote.

A blackout in IRS data also follows a wider pattern of missing data across the Trump administration, which has either stopped collecting or publishing critical information for dozens of federal datasets.

The administration has been accused of withholding, altering, or removing altogether data findings that have not aligned with the president’s agenda, including budget figures for the war in Iran, air quality reports, CDC surveys, and other key data points used to inform policy and public health.

Trump also fired the Bureau of Labor Statistics last year after calling labor market data “rigged.”

News.title: Man City dismantled by Paris St-Germain in breathless Champions League battle
News.content:
When Manchester City play like this what a loss their football will be to the Premier League – and the Champions League – if they are heavily sanctioned later this season.

In what turned out to be a match for the ages, a night of brilliant, unbridled attack, we were treated to the ultimate game of two halves as the back-to-back European champions Paris St-Germain took City apart for 45 minutes. And then were left holding on.

City will hope this is a sign of what is to come in their Premier League fight. But with a different result. After suffering a resounding defeat at the hands of the Premier League’s independent commission, with 114 of the 115 charges against them proven, they maintain their innocence and are mounting an appeal.

Could they make a comeback? It would be incredible and highly improbable if they did so but, out on the pitch, and 3-0 down after a first half in which they were in danger of being humiliated by PSG, they created enough opportunities to save themselves.

The data backed that. City’s expected goals (xG) was 2.57 while PSG’s was 1.83. City had 27 shots to 15 and had more possession and more passes. Enzo Maresca made a triple substitution to devastating effect, especially with the introduction of new signings Ayyoub Bouaddi and Iliman Ndiaye.

In the end they clawed back two goals, both scored by Erling Haaland, who now has 61 in 60 games in this competition – seventh outright in the all-time list, before Ruud van Nistelrooy. And 37 of those for City, overtaking Sergio Agüero’s club record.

News.title: Barcola starts to justify £123m price tag with hat-trick as Liverpool hit LASK for six
News.content:
Of the five Premier League teams in the Champions League this season, Liverpool have the friendliest league-phase fixtures and they can secure back-to-back wins against Austrian side LASK in this evening’s early kick off.

Having already vanquished one of their pot one opponents by beating Atletico Madrid at Anfield, Andoni Iraola’s team really should be targeting one of the top spots.

They travel to Linz without some key players, though. Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai missed the defeat by Manchester City and remain sidelined, while Hugo Ekitike is a long-term absentee.

There were positive aspects to Liverpool’s performance against City, but they collapsed like a deck of cards after Ryan Gravenberch’s harsh second yellow card.

Tonight’s game is one they should dominate, and it is a presentable opportunity for Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola to kick-start their seasons and respond to the recent criticism of their performances. Iraola hopes to have a stronger squad to choose from at the weekend, when Liverpool face a stringent test at Brentford. This is the second of nine matches in 28 days for Liverpool.

“You don’t have a lot of time to train,” said Iraola. “You try to prepare the games now a lot of times just with the videos and the tactics boards, just a little bit outside. You have to prioritise the freshness of the players.

“Especially now we are playing four games in 10 days, it’s keeping all the legs, all the energy in the games.

LASK are currently third in the Austrian league, but booked their place in this season’s Champions League proper with a remarkable comeback from 4-0 down on aggregate against Celtic.

They have injury problems of their own to contend with George Bello and Moses Usor limping off in the weekend’s defeat by league leaders Rapid Wien and Ramiz Harakate tearing his anterior cruciate ligament in July.

They do play on a grass pitch at the Raiffeisen Arena though Kasper Schmeichel, the former Celtic goalkeeper who was working as a TV pundit for the game, was critical of the playing surface.

Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Second Ebola case confirmed in Kenya
News.content:
Kenya has recorded its second-ever case of Ebola after a relative of a patient who died last week tested positive for the virus, officials have said.

A 39-year-old man fell ill on Tuesday and has since been confirmed to be infected with Ebola, according to Kenyan health authorities.

The patient, who is now isolated, is a family member of Kenya’s first-ever Ebola case, who died in a hospital in Nairobi last Monday.

The index case, a 40-year old businessman, had travelled to Kenya from the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), the epicentre of the deadly outbreak of the rare Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, which has so far killed more than 4,300 people.

Kenyan authorities have identified 128 of his contacts and have successfully tracked down 113 of them, who are having their temperatures checked daily for a period of three weeks, the country’s Director-General for Health, Dr Patrick Amoth, said in a statement.

“There is no evidence of spread in the wider community,” the statement, issued on Wednesday, added.

However, questions remain over whether more cases will crop up in the coming weeks.

News.title: I tried Apple’s new smart home hub – the brand faithful will love it
News.content:
HomeView can control smart lights, heating, security cameras and video doorbells via touch or voice, but devices must support Matter – the cross-brand smart home standard. That means you aren’t confined to Apple-approved gadgets, but you are still limited – Ring video doorbells, for example, aren’t Matter-compatible, so they won’t work with HomeView, which could be a deal-breaker for even the biggest Apple fan.

But for anyone put off by the complexity of setting up a smart home, Apple is trying to simplify things. It has partnered with LG on Home Collection – a range of devices, including security cameras and a video doorbell – that connect with a single tap, just as AirPods do with an iPhone. They won’t be available until later in the year, but they could mark a major step towards making smart home set-up less complicated.

My early verdict

HomeView is built for the Apple faithful: set-up requires an iPhone or iPad, personalised AI features need a recent Apple Intelligence-capable iPhone, and some apps work only when your phone is nearby. In a household split between iPhone and Android, Android users will get a much thinner experience, and Apple’s own services come first at every turn.

Still, HomeView is the most polished smart display I have seen. Face recognition makes it both a great shared and personalised device; the sound quality is excellent; and Siri AI is finally worth talking to, especially when it can draw on your personal context. I’ll need to live with it for a few weeks before giving a final verdict, but so far it’s a beautifully designed device I’d be happy to invite into my home.

News.title: Ed Miliband calls for ‘new deal on debt’ as developing countries face spiralling borrowing costs
News.content:
Ed Miliband, the foreign secretary, has called for a “new deal on debt” as spiralling borrowing costs force developing countries to spend more on interest payments than on education or health.

In a speech in Bangkok on Wednesday, Mr Miliband warned that the global financial system is failing emerging markets, and promised to use the UK’s diplomatic heft to push for urgent reform.

He said: “The short-term repayments are crippling, and while many are not defaulting on their payments they are being forced, if you like, to default on the lives and prospects of future generations.

“So we need a new deal on debt, a deal that supports countries to repay over longer time horizons and, crucially, refinancing with better rates to give developing countries precious fiscal space.”

Although public debt is not inherently problematic, servicing costs are at a 25-year-high – squeezing government coffers just as conflict, climate change and a ‘Godzilla’ El Niño push food and fuel prices ever higher.

Emerging economies in particular have little headroom: according to the Rockefeller Foundation, average interest payments now exceed 10 per cent of revenue in developing nations, while UN Trade and Development (UNCTAD) analysis found 3.7 billion people live in countries where debt servicing costs exceed spending on health or education.

At the same time, overseas development aid (ODA) spending from wealthy countries has plummeted – hitting social, infrastructure and humanitarian projects, and disaster response.

The mounting global debt pile has dominated discussions in Bangkok this week, where some 15,000 people have descended for the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank annual meetings.

This included the first meeting of the newly formed Borrowers’ Platform on Monday. A group of finance ministers and central bank governors from some 30 countries, it was formed to exchange ideas about how to deal with debt burdens – and how to avoid pitfalls.

News.title: Trump backs down in Zambia mineral and data-sharing row
News.content:
Zambia has signed a five-year health financing agreement with the US government after the US dropped demands for access to sensitive health data and separated the deal from negotiations over the country’s mineral resources.

The agreement follows months of negotiations over a $2.49 billion health aid package, with Zambia pushing back against US demands to share medical data and give preferential access to the country’s rich mineral reserves in exchange for money to provide lifesaving healthcare.

Under the final agreement, Zambia will not be required to hand over individual patient records or biological specimens, which the US had previously argued was important for global disease surveillance.

Data sharing will be restricted to monitoring and evaluating US-funded health programmes.

A separate agreement covering US access to Zambia’s critical minerals has also been decoupled from the health financing deal, it was confirmed last week.

“The government will not be sharing any specimens with the United States because we removed all those aspects that raised concern,” Zambian Health Minister Roma Chilengi said last week as the agreement was signed.

Zambia’s Foreign Minister Mulambo Haimbe also confirmed that the health and mineral agreements had been separated.

“There was this [memorandum of understanding] on health and another on critical minerals, and we were saying that these need to be decoupled, and this has been done,” he said.

News.title: Progress against HIV stalls in South Africa, research shows
News.content:
South Africa’s progress in tackling the Aids and HIV crisis has stalled in one of its most populous provinces, new research has found.

The number of new cases of the infection in KwaZulu-Natal province, centred around the eastern port of Durban, have stopped falling after years of steep declines.

Data from a long-running study following thousands of people also showed those with detectable levels of virus in their blood had risen slightly despite years of medics prescribing antiretroviral drugs.

Researchers said the peer-reviewed study published in The Lancet HIV medical journal “provides a stark warning on prevailing HIV trends in rural South Africa, where ground is being lost in the fight against the HIV epidemic”.

The researchers, led by scientists at Durban’s Africa Health Research Institute (AHRI) and Stellenbosch University’s South African Centre for Epidemiological Modelling and Analysis (SACEMA), used a 20-year study which has tested nearly 60,000 people.

Analysis showed that after steep reductions in HIV incidence from 2013 to 2018, incidence rates for both males and females showed little or no decrease from 2019 onwards.

Incidence rates had continued to fall for young people under 35, but that had been offset by a lack of progress for those in middle age.

News.title: Carrick’s United are in crisis and now spotlight is on Wilcox
News.content:
They seem to lack players who can play on the front foot, who have the athletic dynamism required in this league and too many self-indulgent forward players who either can’t be bothered to help out their team-mates or cannot concentrate long enough to do so. Spooked by their lack of pace in defence and midfield, they are hidebound by caution, dropping ever deeper, ever more reliant on counter-attacking despite the blatant disconnect between the front four and back six. If they drift through this match and Sunday’s trip to Elland Road, Carrick may join the long list of Ineos-driven managerial mis-steps.

Atlético have won six of eight in La Liga and have been defeated only once. They are five points behind Barcelona in second and have score 18 goals and let in eight, which may seem a curious thing to include in a preview but it is done to emphasise that many fans’ perception of Diego Simeone’s team are out of date. Back in the days of Diego Godín, Gabi, Juanfran et all, six wins a draw and a defeat would have had goals for of about 10 and goals against of maybe three.

Simeone is a martinet about attitude not systems or styles and his team have evolved, with the World Cup-winner Alex Baena, who has scored four goals so far, driving them on. He has reintegrated Julián Alvarez, too, after his brazen attempt to force a move to Barcelona so incensed Atléti fans that it seemed they would drive him out of the club. Simeone refused to let Alvarez get his own way and he is now buckling down. Ten years ago Simeone would have bitten his head off.

Sports.title: Martinez releases statement to clarify outburst - but does not apologise
Sports.content:
Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez has clarified his outburst after Tuesday's Champions League loss at Atletico Madrid in a statement - but stopped short of an apology.

Martinez launched an extraordinary attack on the club's hierarchy after the 2-0 defeat in Madrid, as he criticised the lack of summer investment in the squad, said he expected more from "upstairs" and singled out technical director Jason Wilcox.

But 24 hours on from his astonishing post-match interview, the Argentina international released a statement on Instagram on Wednesday night to clear up his comments.

He said: "Following everything that has been said about my comments yesterday, I want to share some thoughts on what I said and how I feel.

"After the match, I spoke out of anger and frustration at not getting the result we all wanted.

"Those who know me know how I live football, with passion, commitment and a huge desire to win. And when things don't go our way, it hurts, especially when representing a club with the history and stature of Manchester United.

"My words reflect how I feel and how much I want to see this club competing for the biggest honours. Those high standards are part of how I see football and the responsibility that comes with wearing this shirt.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kaveh Solhekol and Rob Dorsett answered your questions about Martinez's post-match outburst

"When I talk about wanting more, I'm talking about the ambition we must all have as part of this club. To keep growing, to become stronger and to have everything we need to compete at the highest level. These are standards we must all hold ourselves to, starting with me.

"I know that, first and foremost, it's us, the players, who have to deliver, and I put myself at the front of that responsibility. We need to demand even more of ourselves and work together to take Manchester United back to the top.

"I believe in my team-mates, our manager and everyone working to help this club move forward. I'm convinced that the way forward is to keep working together, with ambition and commitment.

"My goal has been the same since day one, to win, to compete at the highest level and to give everything I have for this badge."

Sky Sports News' Football Correspondent Rob Dorsett:

There are real doubts about whether Martinez's contract will be extended when it expires in the summer.

United will focus on revamping their defence in the next transfer windows and have the formal option to prolong Martinez's stay for a further year.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jamie O'Hara criticised Martinez following comments made by the defender aimed at the Manchester United hierarchy

Sky Sports News has also been told United are looking at new centre-backs, as well as left-backs.

United's bosses have yet to decide whether to discipline Martinez for his comments, when he said: "I expect more from our technical director [meaning director of football, Jason Wilcox]. We expect more from the top, from upstairs, to bring in more players to compete."

Sky Sports News has been told there is anger and bemusement at what Martinez said, both in the United boardroom and in the changing room, with at least one other player challenging him over his comments as the squad got on board the plane to fly back to Manchester.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Soccer Special pundits react to Lisandro Martinez's comments aimed at Manchester United's hierarchy after their Champions League defeat to Atletico Madrid.

It is also understood that there is no pressure on Wilcox internally regarding his position.

The implication that Martinez doesn't think his team-mates are good enough to compete has not gone down well with other players.

Martinez has been keen on a move away from Old Trafford for some time.

In the summer, he pushed for a move to Atletico Madrid, the side that beat United in the Champions League on Tuesday night, to follow his good friend and international team-mate, Cristian Romero, who left Spurs for Spain.

No suitable bid for Martinez came in for Manchester United to consider.

The 28-year-old made similar explosive comments about his bosses when at Ajax in 2022. Martinez, who again wanted a move away, called their sporting director Gerry Hamstra a "nobody".

Martinez remains a key part of Michael Carrick's squad and United's bosses know they have to handle this situation carefully.

Sports.title: Man City beaten by PSG in thriller as Guardiola returns to Etihad
Sports.content:
Manchester City were beaten 4-2 by a majestic Paris Saint-Germain as Pep Guardiola watched on from the stands in an enthralling Champions League encounter.

The reigning back-to-back European champions were keen to make their power felt early at the Etihad, in a game that made clear where the greater concentration of quality resides. Luis Enrique's side were breathtaking in the first half, a masterclass in effortless control with and without the ball.

Desire Doue scored from range. Ousmane Dembele rounded off a wonderful team move 99 seconds later. And Vitinha finished a brilliant first 45 minutes with a thumping finish from Warren Zaire-Emery's instinctive flick. "If you don't go toe-to-toe, you struggle," reflected Enzo Maresca.

Image: Former Man City manager Pep Guardiola was in the stands for the first time since leaving the club

A pair of Erling Haaland goals made the scoreline respectable after the interval, and City were good value for both breakthroughs, doing to PSG what had been done to them in the first period. They hit the woodwork a further two times in a half that became increasingly more frantic and transitional.

Despite wave after wave of attack and big chances missed, it was Gianluigi Donnarumma who failed to escape the glare of the spotlight, his poor handling gifting Maghnes Akliouche and the visitors a fourth. He atoned by denying Ferran Torres' woeful penalty attempt late on.

PSG's first-half blitz proved decisive and sobered the atmosphere around a fairly muted Etihad, but Maresca will take comfort from the way his side turned a would-be rout into a thrilling clash of titans.

Image: Man City stage an inquest after conceding three first-half goals

PSG come out on top in battle of recent winners

As well as being two of the earliest clubs to fall foul of UEFA's financial rules back in 2014, Man City and PSG shared one other thing in common before combining to win three of the past four Champions League titles: They had won none of the previous 67.

Each lost their first Champions League final - PSG to Bayern in 2020 and City the following year to Chelsea. But with both clubs backed by free-spending owners from the Middle East, boasting some of the most talented squads in world football, that deficiency has since become a surplus.

With City now fighting against charges of financial rule-breaking on a domestic front, all of which the club deny, the decision was made for a show of unity on home turf. Guardiola was flanked by high-ranking executives in the terraces, including Chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak and chief executive Ferran Soriano.

Image: Manchester City Chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak and CEO Ferran Soriano in the stands before kick off

They will have seen plenty they liked on the pitch, City's players appearing laser-focused on the job at hand despite the cloud of uncertainty that surrounds them. Ultimately, this is a defeat of fairly insignificant jeopardy where chances and goals made for a superb watch between two European contenders.

The world of football will continue to tune in to see how City handle whatever might come next. Whenever that might be.

A difficult night to make sense of!

Image: Haaland hangs his head after defeat to PSG

Sky Sports' Ben Ransom at the Etihad:

Where do you start trying to make sense of that?

Pep Guardiola was back for a bonkers night, with his former side showing plenty of the strengths and weaknesses that displayed themselves in different ways during his tenure. The City fightback at least means his visit won't be characterised by a humbling defeat.

PSG were the better side overall and deserved the win, but on another night the scoreline could have been reversed, given the number of chances that went begging for the home side.

The City fans might not get to see their side in this competition next year, but as they made clear before kick-off, this is a fanbase that has stood by the club during dark times before, and is promising to do so again.

Maresca believes City can match PSG

Man City boss Enzo Maresca:

"It was a strange game. Two goals in two minutes created some problems for us. We were dead in the game, and then second half we created so many chances. Second half, we were good.

"We lost a bit of balance, distance between players, and we struggle first half. Second half we made changes and adjusted some things, then we were much better. These kind of teams, if you don't go toe-to-toe you struggle. We had to be more brave. Second half, we were.

"We are there, to be honest. My feeling is that we are close. It's already difficult against PSG, but then you concede two quick goals. We can learn from that and move on."

Man City's next fixtures...

Sports.title: Barcola scores hat-trick as Liverpool thrash LASK
Sports.content:
Bradley Barcola scored a hat-trick and Florian Wirtz shone after recent criticism as Liverpool thrashed LASK 6-3 to earn their second win in the Champions League.

Barcola kick-started his Liverpool career, having not scored or assisted in six appearances since his £123m move from Paris Saint-Germain, while Wirtz responded to calls for him to be dropped with a fine performance in what was expected to be a comfortable evening against the Austrian Bundesliga champions.

Liverpool had 19 shots in the opening period, a new record for an away team in the first half of a Champions League game, as Ronald Araujo headed in his first goal for the club before Barcola got off the mark with a tidy finish and then slotted in another from a Wirtz pass.

Andoni Iraola's side were relentless with Trey Nyoni, 19, impressing in midfield alongside Ryan Gravenberch and they helped add a fourth when Jeremie Frimpong met Kostas Tsimikas' cross with an excellent header that went in off the post just six minutes after the break.

Iraola benched Virgil van Dijk in Austria for only the third time in Liverpool's 39 Champions League games since 2022, but when he and Joe Gomez were introduced at centre-back in the 62nd minute, they conceded three times.

Barcola's hat-trick, a tap-in from Frimpong's cross, followed Robert Ljubicic's consolation before Wales striker Lewis Koumas, leading the line in Alexander Isak's absence, deservedly scored Liverpool's sixth after he had two efforts ruled out for offside.

Florian Flecker reduced the deficit late on with two clinical finishes in two minutes, exposing Liverpool's sloppy defending to take some shine off the victory.

The key moments from a goal-fest...

22: GOAL! Liverpool get their reward after a strong start as Araujo climbs highest at a corner to head in his first goal for the club.

Liverpool get their reward after a strong start as Araujo climbs highest at a corner to head in his first goal for the club. 24: TWO IN TWO MINUTES! Barcola calmly slots in from 12 yards for his first Liverpool goal.

Barcola calmly slots in from 12 yards for his first Liverpool goal. 31: OFFSIDE! Liverpool striker Koumas has his well-taken finish ruled out for offside.

Liverpool striker Koumas has his well-taken finish ruled out for offside. 33: OFF THE WOODWORK! Liverpool are threatening to run riot as Gravenberch strikes the inside of the right post.

Liverpool are threatening to run riot as Gravenberch strikes the inside of the right post. 37: BARCOLA AGAIN! Wirtz has been at the heart of Liverpool's superb first-half performance and he threads a pass through for Barcola to score.

Wirtz has been at the heart of Liverpool's superb first-half performance and he threads a pass through for Barcola to score. 51: GOAL! Liverpool get their fourth as Frimpong meets Tsimikas' cross with a superb header that goes in off the post.

Liverpool get their fourth as Frimpong meets Tsimikas' cross with a superb header that goes in off the post. 53: OFFSIDE FLAG 2-0 KOUMAS! The Liverpool striker is denied again by the flag after finding the net.

The Liverpool striker is denied again by the flag after finding the net. 62: SUBS! Van Dijk and Gomez come on at the back for Jeremy Jacquet and Ronald Araujo.

Van Dijk and Gomez come on at the back for Jeremy Jacquet and Ronald Araujo. 63: GOAL! Liverpool's new centre-back pairing concede instantly as Ljubicic strikes.

Liverpool's new centre-back pairing concede instantly as Ljubicic strikes. 66: HAT-TRICK! Barcola gets his third and it is his easiest of the night, tapping in from just yards out.

Barcola gets his third and it is his easiest of the night, tapping in from just yards out. 72: KOUMAS GETS HIS GOAL! He wasn't to be denied and finally Koumas can celebrate for real following his close-range finish.

He wasn't to be denied and finally Koumas can celebrate for real following his close-range finish. 75: GOAL! Flecker stoops to turn in Dibango's cross.

Flecker stoops to turn in Dibango's cross. 77: GOAL! It's Flecker again! Twice in two minutes he capitalises on poor defending to find the net.

Iraola praises Barcola and Wirtz but criticises defence

Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola:

On Barcola: "I think he played so well today and not just the goals. He had more chances to score, he was always a threat attacking the spaces in behind. In training, sometimes you feel when a player is in the zone, and fortunately tonight for us, he has shown the level that he has."

On Wirtz: "I think he was amazing in possession. I think he had lively passes, good assists, he helped us to control the game. Especially in the first half where he was roaming around and finding good spots. It was a good game from Florian."

On defence: "Probably the reason why the manager shouldn't change both centre-backs, but we were already winning 4-0 and you have to think about the next game and saving the legs of the players. We didn't defend properly at the end of the game."

Liverpool defence dampens big win

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lee Hendrie felt Liverpool's 6-3 win against LASK was a 'great result' but admits he was concerned by the their defence.

Sky Sports' David Richardson:

On a night when so much went right for Liverpool, some defensive concerns remained. More worryingly, the problems began when experienced duo Virgil van Dijk and Joe Gomez came on, replacing the untested partnership of Jeremy Jacquet and Ronald Araujo.

Finding balance in this Liverpool side was a factor in Arne Slot's dismissal and something Andoni Iraola has struggled with early in his time at the club.

The attack hasn't been free-flowing this season either, creating just nine big chances in the Premier League, the fewest of any team alongside Aston Villa and Coventry, but it clicked in Austria, albeit against weaker opposition.

Bradley Barcola will hope he has ignited his Liverpool career while Florian Wirtz delivered a confidence-boosting performance and Lewis Koumas' goal will help him grow in stature.

Liverpool are still very much a work in progress as Iraola finds a formula to blend his big-money signings with a new style of play.

Liverpool's next fixtures...

Sports.title: Quickfire Doué and Dembélé inspire PSG to thrilling win at Manchester City
Sports.content:
A penny for Pep Guardiola’s thoughts. The legendary Manchester City manager was back at the Etihad Stadium for the first time since his departure at the end of last season and, well, the announcement of you-know-what.

Sporting a flat cap, Guardiola took his seat in the stands behind the City chair, Khaldoon al-Mubarak, and the chief executive, Ferran “Not” Soriano, and, certainly, the TV director seemed intent on scrutinising him – if the number of cutaway shots to him were any guide.

Everybody knows where Guardiola stands on the great City scandal; the numerous guilty verdicts handed down to them on the 100-plus charges they have faced for breaking the Premier League’s financial rules. He has backed his former employers to somehow disprove them. But what did he make of his old team here against the might of the defending European champions, Paris Saint-Germain?

Not much in the first half would have been a reasonable conclusion. PSG played football from a higher plane and they might have led by more than the three unanswered goals they scored. But if defiance has been the theme for City – and it fed into Guardiola’s presence here – they produced plenty more of it during a thrilling second half.

City refused to accept the inevitable. They threw everything at PSG. Erling Haaland ran on adrenaline as City created a flurry of openings. The No 9 was unplayable at times; he finished with two goals and a few near misses. City were a goal away from worrying PSG.

The problem for them was the one that Maghnes Akliouche scored to put PSG 4-1 in front. It meant that City’s dream of an astonishing fightback was only an illusion. What a terrible concession it was for Gianluigi Donnarumma – and not for the first time.

View image in fullscreen The former City manager Pep Guardiola takes his seat at the Etihad. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

It was a spin and blast from Akliouche on the edge of the area and Donnarumma appeared to have palmed the ball up and away. Except that it dropped all the way back down – quite a way back down – and into the net. How did it happen? It was one of many head-scratchers; the sheer weight of chances was difficult to process. PSG even threw in a late penalty fail by Ferran Torres, who came on as a substitute; his kick was weak and too close to Donnarumma. Are you missing it all, Pep?

City must play under a cloud, certainly until their appeal against the charges is completed, and they ran into a PSG team that shimmered with menace. Luis Enrique’s starting XI featured seven players who are on the 30-strong Ballon d’Or shortlist. The manager had another three from it among his substitutes, including João Neves and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.

PSG bristled with their trademark assurance on the ball; the beautifully grooved combinations. It does not matter how tight the spaces are. They back themselves to get out of them. Witness the opening goal and a scintillating piece of team play that began deep on the right-hand side of their defensive third.

In the blink of an eye, PSG were surging up the flank and then opening out the move, Fabián Ruiz playing the final pass to Désiré Doué on the left. The winger cut inside and shot low for the near corner from outside the area. It was the precision that did for Donnarumma, although the former PSG goalkeeper had to do better at his post.

View image in fullscreen Ousmane Dembélé doubles PSG’s lead in the first half. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

When PSG landed the follow-up punch just 75 seconds later, City were reeling, the home crowd stunned. It was a goal that featured two crosses, the first from Ousmane Dembélé out to Doué on the left. He took the ball down and crossed back for Dembélé, who stole in behind Marc Guéhi. The run was too cute, the header straightforward.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

It was no exaggeration to say that PSG could have had five by the interval. City had no defence to their cut and thrust; the sheer pace of it, the positional fluidity too. Achraf Hakimi appeared to be playing almost anywhere but right-back. He popped up inside the six-yard box in the 32nd minute only to send a free header against the post, but City were swiftly disabused of the notion that the danger had passed.

View image in fullscreen Vitinha sweeps home PSG’s third before the interval. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

PSG won the ball back and went for the jugular once again. Akliouche was involved, there was a lovely backheeled assist from Warren Zaïre-Emery and Vitinha lashed home a low drive. When Hakimi blew a one-on-one with Donnarumma on 39 minutes, it felt as though his team were toying with City.

Enzo Maresca made a triple change at the interval, introducing Matheus Nunes, Ayyoub Bouaddi and Iliman Ndiaye – and the effect was immediate. City played with devil-may-care abandon. Their toothless first half was forgotten. Enzo Fernández blew a gilt-edged headed opportunity and Ndiaye worked Matvey Safonov before Haaland pulled one back. It was a whipped ball in from Ndiaye, which Haaland sent into the far corner with a flex of the neck muscles. He was not close in, either.

Could City take the lifeline? Antoine Semenyo ran through and dinked against the crossbar. The offside flag was raised, although he looked to have been level. City needed the next goal to make it interesting. Instead, they lost the initiative after another Donnarumma lapse.

It was the prompt for a whirlwind finale. Josko Gvardiol saw a header cleared off the line by Nuno Mendes, Fernández rattled the outside of a post and Haaland looped a header against the top of the crossbar before he scored again – a low finish after good work from Bouaddi. Haaland was denied the hat-trick when he stretched to prod at Nunes’ cross at goal – it was an excellent save by Safonov – and City finished with 27 shots and 52 touches in the opposition box. Those numbers would be enough for victory on most nights. Just not this one.

Sports.title: ‘I expect more’: the key questions from Martínez’s Manchester United broadside | Jamie Jackson
Sports.content:
After Manchester United’s 2-0 loss at Atlético Madrid, Lisandro Martínez teed off at the director of football, Jason Wilcox, and the rest of the executive. “We don’t have the best squad at the moment compared with other top teams,” said the defender. “I expect more [investment], 100%. I expect more from our technical director [Jason Wilcox] … Really poor [the Atlético defeat] – I have to control myself a lot but something is a reflection of the mirror of how our club is at the moment.” Here we consider the key questions emerging from Martínez’s explosive remarks.

Is Martínez’s view reflective of the squad generally?

Yes is the short answer. The Guardian has been told the decision to target three midfielders in Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and Carlos Baleba caused bemusement in the squad that no other areas were strengthened in the summer. Carrick led United to third last term after the side only had 17 league games remaining when he took over in January, having been eliminated from the other competitions. The need for defensive reinforcements is particularly acute because the back four of Diogo Dalot, Martínez, Harry Maguire and Luke Shaw has been together since 2022. Martínez is out of contract next summer and it is thought the 28-year-old may not be offered a new deal or have his one-year option triggered by the club, so teammates are conscious his outburst also came because he expects to leave.

How culpable is Wilcox?

As United’s director of football the 55-year-old wields near-unilateral power on football decisions, with only Sir Jim Ratcliffe, who controls sporting policy, above him. If the buck stops with the executive, the most recent transfer window was Wilcox’s responsibility. This was the latest in a line of missteps on his United record. One concerns when Dan Ashworth (Wilcox’s predecessor) was on gardening leave from Newcastle in the first half of 2024, Wilcox interviewed potential replacements for Erik ten Hag before, oddly, deeming that the head coach should stay. The Dutchman signed a fresh contract but was sacked that autumn. Another involves Wilcox’s major falling out with the man he hired as the Dutchman’s successor, Ruben Amorim, after which the Portuguese said the director of football had told him he should change his favoured 3-4-3 shape. “I came here to be the manager of Manchester United – not to be the coach of Manchester United,” said Amorim, after a 1-1 draw at Leeds on 4 January (his job title was head coach). He was sacked the next day. Wilcox worked with Omar Berrada, United’s chief executive, at Manchester City, where Berrada rose to become chief football operations officer, and Wilcox became academy director. Wilcox moved to Southampton and became director of football from summer 2023 until April 2024, when he joined United, having been identified by Berrada, so there is scrutiny of his experience at elite level.

View image in fullscreen Lisandro Martínez’s post-match interview has exposed the divisions at Manchester United. Photograph: Ash Donelon/Manchester United/Getty Images

How much blame is Carrick’s?

The 45-year-old’s ability to prosper is related to the quality of Wilcox’s work, primarily in the market, so he cannot be solely responsible for a dire six points from six league games and two victories in all competitions all season. Yet by definition his role as head coach demands Carrick do the best with his resources, and that progress is made on the training ground. On matchdays there is scant excuse for United’s disjointedness, inferior running stats and inability, twice, to take advantage against 10 men: the 1-0 loss to City and Saturday’s 1-1 draw with Tottenham. How is Carrick viewed by his players? According to Santos they back him. “We believe in the manager, we believe in the whole staff, we believe in [ourselves as] players,” he said after the Atlético game. “We are in a bad moment but we have to work to change this result.”.

Is United’s unity and discipline crumbling?

For further evidence see Amad Diallo’s Snapchat post after the defeat by Atlético: “Fucking disgrace; I have no words.” So United have a World Cup-winner, Martínez, aiming shots at Wilcox and by implication Ratcliffe and Berrada, and a fellow senior player, Diallo, cursing but in ambiguous fashion, adding to the sense of meltdown at the club because it is unclear whether the “disgrace” meant the performance, Martínez’s diatribe, the squad his teammate referred to as not good enough, or something else. All of this is mirrored on the pitch, where United’s 671.4km run in the Premier League is the fifth-lowest (Arsenal’s 716.2 is the highest), and their 581 sprints the fourth-lowest (Brentford’s 765 the most).

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Michael Carrick has support from his squad but Manchester United’s form has dropped significantly this season. Photograph: Susana Vera/Reuters

Where are the Glazers in all this?

In mitigation Wilcox can point to the six American siblings, who remain majority owners and whose family has placed an eye-watering £1.1bn-plus debt on the club that severely restricts the transfer budget. Wilcox oversaw a £155m summer outlay and a net spend of about £100m in a summer when City’s corresponding figures were £457.5m and about £175m. City buying players such as Enzo Fernández (for a British record-equalling £125m), Elliot Anderson (£115m), Ayyoub Bouaddi (£81m) and Iliman Ndiaye (£65m) showed their greater financial muscle, helped by being much better sellers of talent. How they have reached this point has, though, been thrown into sharp focus by last month’s verdict that they have serially cheated.

Are there positives for United?

Any straw should be clutched at so Carrick and his staff can view the first 97 minutes of Baleba’s United career as a rosy augury. After entering on 59 minutes against Spurs, a cute swivel and deft chip to Bruno Fernandes was a moment as impressive as the rest of his debut, and at Atlético the 22-year-old hunted down opponents and crunched into tackles, suggesting his game contains energy, muscularity and skill. It’s early days but perhaps if Baleba had been fit to start the campaign (he was recovering from an ankle problem) he might have affected one or more of the defeat at Hull, the 2-2 draw at Everton when Ainsley Maitland-Niles equalised late, the 1-0 loss to City when Phil Foden was sent off after 23 minutes or the Carabao Cup elimination by Brighton.

Sports.title: Jackson and Barkley doubles sink feeble Fenerbahce in record Aston Villa win
Sports.content:
It may be a bit early for the pantomime season but the Holte End enjoyed acclaiming their heroes and villains as Aston Villa won at home for the first time this season with their biggest victory in European competition. Every touch for Mason Greenwood, playing his first game in England since January 2022, was booed, but even louder applause was reserved for Aston Villa’s rediscovered attacking prowess.

Johan Manzambi celebrated his 21st birthday by opening the scoring on his first Champions League appearance, before Nicolas Jackson took the game beyond Fenerbahce’s reach with two more goals before half-time to help banish any fears about playing in front of the demolished North Stand.

With Prince William cheering on from the stands, Ross Barkley made this a night to remember as he scored twice, the first goal from a penalty earned by Manzambi, and Tammy Abraham helped Villa score six in a game for the first time since beating Brighton in 2023. No team has won more games (15) in European competition since the start of last season.

Villa’s supposed hex about playing in front of the empty North Stand was put to bed as they scored three times at the end of the ground that is being redeveloped this winter. “Greenwood, Greenwood, what’s the score,” echoed around the three packed stands at Villa Park. Chants of a less salubrious nature were also given regular renditions. This was the former England forward’s first game in this country since he played in Manchester United’s 1-0 win against West Ham United in nearly five years ago.

View image in fullscreen Johan Manzambi scores his deflected goal for the opener. Photograph: Tim Keeton/EPA

Greenwood was charged in 2022 with attempted rape, controlling and coercive behaviour and assault occasioning actual bodily harm. The Crown Prosecution Service discontinued the case in February 2023 after key witnesses withdrew their involvement and new material came to light. The player had denied the charges.

He had played for Marseille in a friendly against Villa 14 months ago, when he allegedly spat at Amadou Onana. So it was no surprise when his name was booed as the teams were announced and at every subsequent involvement.

Far more palatable was the freedom with which Villa played. Jackson now has five goals for Unai Emery’s team since signing from Chelsea for £65m in the summer while Manzambi, a £59.5m capture from Freiburg, was a joy to watch in the No 10 role, combining deft touch with wiry physicality. “My first Champions League game and my first goal, on my birthday,” he said. “My family are here. That’s very nice for me.”

The Switzerland international composed himself to score after Mattéo Guendouzi had inadvertently headed on John McGinn’s cross following a short corner.

Zion Suzuki twice saved well from Vedat Muriqi but Villa created umpteen chances themselves. Jackson, collecting Boubacar Kamara’s pass, struck home cleanly from the edge of the penalty area just after the half-hour mark before repeating the trick six minutes before the interval. In between, Oguz Aydin shot against the Villa bar, but, truth be told, Villa’s 11th successive home win in European competitions was already safely banked.

Villa’s free-scoring spell is in stark contrast to their start to the season, when they only managed one goal in their opening four games. Now they have scored at least three times in four of their past six matches.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Should they beat Viking here next Wednesday, Villa would be well on their way to qualifying from the league stage with nine points from three games. “We are being ambitious,” Unai Emery, the Villa manager, said. “We want to be protagonists in the Champions League.”

View image in fullscreen Nicolas Jackson drills the ball between Nathan Aké’s legs to score Aston Villa’s third. Photograph: Andrew Boyers/Action Images/Reuters

Manzambi was tripped by Ismail Yuksek midway through the second half for the penalty from which Barkley made it 4-0, even if Jackson admitted he had fancied the chance to keep the match ball. “Yeah I wanted to take it but the most important thing is we win,” the striker told TNT Sports. “Hopefully next time I’ll get the hat-trick.”

The cheers that followed that goal were promptly matched by the jeers for Greenwood as he was substituted. The pantomime was over as a contest.

Barkley swiftly added a fifth with a deflected shot. But even before Abraham turned in Alysson’s cross for the sixth goal, some Villa minds were turning to Saturday evening’s trip to Newcastle United and the perennial autumnal challenge of resurrecting a difficult start to the league season. In Emery they trust.

Sports.title: Bradley Barcola’s clinical hat-trick inspires Liverpool to 6-3 rout of Lask
Sports.content:
Liverpool cleansed themselves from the stains of defeat by Manchester City at the earliest opportunity. A rampant display in Austria saw Bradley Barcola ignite his Liverpool account with the first hat-trick of his professional career and Andoni Iraola’s team devastate Lask’s big night in the Champions League. The major surprise was how the hosts managed to score three.

Iraola’s pre-match faith in the big-money signings Barcola and Florian Wirtz was repaid as the pair helped dismantle limited opponents. But it was not all about the money and the £123m signing from Paris Saint-Germain scoring the first goals of his Liverpool career. Lewis Koumas registered his first goal in the competition and replaced Steven Gerrard as the youngest player to score and assist in a Champions League game for Liverpool. A total of 26 shots equalled Liverpool’s record in a Champions League away game.

“I’m really happy for Bradley,” said the Liverpool head coach. “Yesterday you were asking me a lot about his numbers, and also Flo [Wirtz], and both of them played really well. They made a difference. Apart from the hat-trick Bradley was a threat one-v-one, helped us control the game and defended the pockets. It will do their confidence good for sure.”

The home end was full and in strong voice over an hour before kick-off as Lask supporters came to savour their club’s first home game in the Champions League proper. The Lask team proved to be much less impressive though, in fairness to the Austrian crowd, their support rarely wavered even as a rout unfolded before their eyes. Liverpool revelled in their superiority and the invitation to recover from Sunday’s first defeat of the season.

Iraola rested Virgil van Dijk, delaying the defender’s 200th game as Liverpool captain, and Alexis Mac Allister as he managed workloads ahead of Saturday’s visit to Brentford. A new-look central defence of Ronald Araújo and Jérémy Jacquet were given a physical test by the Lask strikers Samuel Adeniran and Krystof Danek but handled the host’s rudimental approach comfortably.

View image in fullscreen Bradley Barcola slides the ball into the bottom corner to score his second in the first half. Photograph: Dénes Erdős/AP

Liverpool were utterly dominant against an opponent that struggled to retain possession in all areas of the pitch. The breakthrough was inevitable but also a result of a mix-up in the Lask defence between Alemão and the goalkeeper, Lukas Jungwirth. From the second corner that followed their error, Araújo towered above his marker to head home Kostas Tsimikas’s delivery. It was the Uruguay international’s first Liverpool goal and the start of an onslaught.

Merely 96 seconds later it was 2-0 as Barcola also scored his first Liverpool goal. The summer recruit found himself under scrutiny ahead of the game, along with Wirtz, having gone six appearances for his new club without a goal or an assist. That issue was put to bed when Rio Ngumoha weaved in from the right and Koumas laid the ball back to the lurking winger. Barcola swept a first-time shot inside Jungwirth’s far post. Liverpool were enjoying themselves.

Wirtz soon found himself with a much-needed assist for Barcola’s second goal. The Germany international has looked more at home for Liverpool in the Champions League than Premier League and this was no exception. Wirtz picked out Barcola’s run into the Lask area and the winger rolled a cool finish beyond the exposed keeper.

Lask could have been seriously embarrassed before half-time. Koumas had a fine finish disallowed for offside and, following another neat exchange between Wirtz and Barcola, Ryan Gravenberch’s shot kissed the inside of the far post. Liverpool’s 19 attempts on goal were the most by an away side in the first half of a Champions League game since records began in 2003-04.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Liverpool’s Lewis Koumas jumps for joy after opening his Champions League account. Photograph: Michael Zemanek/Shutterstock

There would be no letup from Iraola’s team after the interval. Jeremie Frimpong morphed into an old-fashioned centre-forward to rise above Yvan Dibango and bury a textbook header into the bottom corner from Tsimikas’s cross. Koumas had a second goal disallowed for offside before Alisson’s clean sheet was ruined by the Lask substitute Robert Ljubicic sweeping home inside his near post. Barcola was presented with his hat-trick when Ngumoha released Frimpong and the full-back flashed a low cross through the Lask six-yard box. Barcola applied a simple finish at the back post.

Frimpong also supplied the assist for Koumas’s deserved goal, converted from close range after the home side were caught playing out from the back. The Lask substitute Florian Flecker brought a touch of respectability to the scoreline with two goals in four minutes, both set up by Dibango, but there was no disguising the emphatic manner of Liverpool’s victory nor the surge of confidence it should give to Barcola.

Sports.title: Champions League: Mourinho’s Real Madrid stage wild comeback on Roma return
Sports.content:
José Mourinho enjoyed a Roma reunion to remember as Real Madrid completed an astonishing comeback by scoring three late goals to claim a 4-3 away win in the Champions League on Wednesday.

Marten de Roon gave the hosts a deserved opener before Kylian Mbappé struck back on his 100th Champions League appearance to level the scores at the break. Two Donyell Malen strikes in the space of six minutes early in the second half seemed to take the game away from the 15-time European champions as Roma ran rampant.

But Madrid scored three goals in the final six minutes, all stemming from corners, to turn the game on its head as Carlos Espí, Endrick and the former Roma defender Antonio Rüdiger struck at a stunned Stadio Olimpico.

Mourinho was a popular figure as he led Roma to the Conference League title and Europa League final during two-and-a-half years in charge. The Portuguese coach was honoured with banners and chants by the home crowd in Roma’s first home Champions League match in more than seven years.

View image in fullscreen José Mourinho is given a hero’s welcome on his return to Roma. Photograph: Alessandra Tarantino/AP

The Real Madrid winger Vinícius Júnior, who featured in the win, was handed a four-match ban for pulling an opponent’s hair during Saturday’s league win over Villarreal. The decision was announced shortly before the game kicked off in Rome – a situation that left Mourinho furious with Spain’s football authorities.

“They do things shamelessly now,” Mourinho said. The cat is out of the bag now. Two hours before the match, a player must know he has a four-match suspension. Couldn’t they do it now? Couldn’t they do it tomorrow morning? Do we have to come by bus and almost arrive at the stadium when we find out?”

Fredrik Sjøvold’s 52nd-minute strike secured a 1-0 victory for Bodø/Glimt over Borussia Dortmund, extending the Norwegian side’s remarkable home record against Europe’s elite.

Bodø were a cut above the 2024 Champions League runners-up and took the lead through Sjøvold just after the break. Dortmund improved in the final half hour but were unable to strike back, despite a late chance for Felix Nmecha.

“There’s nothing we can complain about, we deserved to lose,” said the Dortmund coach, Niko Kovac. “We didn’t bring enough passion today – that’s something Bodø did much better. They took the lead and after that we woke up, but by then it was too late.”

View image in fullscreen Fredrik Sjøvold celebrates after scoring what proved to be the winner for Bodø/Glimt. Photograph: NTB/Reuters

Dortmund join Manchester City, Inter and Sporting as recent big-name scalps on the artificial turf of Bodø’s Aspmyra Stadium. Bodø’s run to the last 16 last season was underpinned by an excellent record at their 8,200-capacity home, officially the smallest venue in this year’s competition.

Nomadic Ukrainian champions Shakhtar Donetsk celebrated moving into their new Champions League “home” at Stamford Bridge by storming back to beat AEK Athens 3-1.

The Greek side took the lead in the 28th minute through Lovro Majer but Pedrinho levelled confidently from the penalty spot just six minutes later. With about 10 minutes of normal time to go, Vinicius Tobias found the net from a tight angle and the substitute Gleiker Mendoza made the game safe, smashing home after cutting in from the left.

Shakhtar, from the east of Ukraine, are using Chelsea’s ground as the base for their European fixtures this season, with the Londoners absent from continental competition.

View image in fullscreen Shakhtar Donetsk fans make themselves at home at Stamford Bridge. Photograph: Kirsty Wigglesworth/AP

Since the beginning of Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, the UK has provided refuge to 265,000 Ukrainians, according to the Ukrainian embassy in London. Fans from the expat population turned out in force on Wednesday, swelling the crowd to 29,000.

Isco scored the winner and Abde Ezzalzouli netted a contender for goal of the week as Real Betis defeated Porto 3-2 in a bad-tempered game in Seville.

Ezzalzouli struck the ball from the corner of the penalty area into the top corner at the far post after the break. Gabriel Veiga equalised with a fine free-kick and set off a kerfuffle between rival players with his celebration. Three players were booked.

The Porto substitute Samu Aghehowa – a Spain international – scored just two minutes after coming on, only for Cucho Hernández – another substitute – to equalise in the 74th. Isco got the winner late with a penalty.

Stuttgart continued their 100% record in this season’s league phase with a 3-0 win against Slovan Bratislava in Slovakia. Earlier, Anis Hadj Moussa scored twice as the Dutch leaders, Feyenoord, came from behind to beat visiting Como 3-2.

Sports.title: Championship roundup: Soucek doubles up as West Ham hit nine-man Lincoln for six
Sports.content:
West Ham returned to winning ways as they cruised to a 6-0 Championship victory against nine-man Lincoln at the ProAmpac Stadium.

The hosts had Tom Hamer sent off after just three minutes and Conor McGrandles followed him off the pitch 20 minutes later, with Konstantinos Mavropanos heading West Ham ahead on the stroke of half-time.

The second half was dominated by West Ham, with further goals coming from Edvin Austbø, Jarrod Bowen, Pablo and Tomas Soucek, who scored twice, as the beleaguered home side desperately tried to keep the score down.

“I credit Lincoln as even with one man down, they were in the game and still creating a lot of problems for us,” said the West Ham manager, Nuno Espírito Santo, after watching his club’s biggest away win for 103 years.

“I think we made mistakes in terms of trying to rush things,” Nuno added. “It changed after the second goal and we played much better, in terms of being patient, recycling the ball and being clinical.”

Southampton recorded their second hard-fought 1-0 win in the space of four days as they condemned their hosts, Norwich, to a fourth successive league defeat.

Tonda Eckert’s side followed up Sunday’s victory over their local rivals, Portsmouth, with their first away win of the campaign in the league, with Kuryu Matsuki scorijng what proved to be the winner early in the second half.

Southampton are now well-placed in the top half of the table after 10 games, despite starting the campaign with a four-point deduction, while Norwich remain too close to the bottom for comfort after another disappointing display.

“To be fair there have been some good performances away from home when we just needed to finish better, ” Eckert said. “Tonight we have put in another good performance and on this occasion, we have got our reward. I am very happy for the boys because they worked very hard out there.”

Ebou Adams scored an 89th-minute winner as Portsmouth recovered after giving away a 2-0 lead to beat 10-man Sheffield United 3-2 at Fratton Park.

The hosts had been in cruise control after Zak Swanson’s stunning blast into the top corner and Adrian Segecic’s tap-in either side of Hamza Choudhury’s dismissal for two bookings. But Japhet Tanganga and Tom Cannon levelled the score and the visitors were somehow hunting back-to-back victories for the first time this season.

View image in fullscreen Southampton manager Tonda Eckert celebrates with his players after their 1-0 win at Norwich. Photograph: Nigel French/PA

Adams had the last word when he jumped off the bench to convert with a minute to go to give Portsmouth their third win of the campaign. After the game, Sheffield United manager Chris Wilder criticised referee Oliver Langford for his decision to send Choudhury off.

“There were a number of decisions which were incredibly frustrating,” Wilder said. “That is three players that have been sent off in the last two games he [Langford] has refereed us. Where are the young and up-and-coming referees who would be refereeing in the Championship now, instead of the ones that are just surviving?

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“No doubt we will have another survivor ref on Saturday. Where is the quality? Where are the ones coming through?” Wilder added. It is a tough one for the players, but there is more frustration and anger towards somebody. We have to deal with it.”

The Portsmouth head coach, John Mousinho, was frustrated by his team’s display despite their late winner. “I am happy that we won the game but the nature and circumstances of it … we have a large amount to learn and a long way to come.
