Sports.title: Formula 1 teams need decision ‘by mid-October’ on whether final races will go ahead | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Formula 1 team bosses say they need to know by the middle of this month whether the series’ final two races will go ahead as planned.

Qatar and Abu Dhabi are due to hold the final two races of the season in November and December. However the war in Iran, which forced the cancellation of races in nearby Bahrain and Saudi Arabia six months ago, put those plans in jeopardy.

F1 has a back-up plan to hold an alternative event at Imola. F1 CEO Stefano Domenicali previously said a decision would be made by mid-September. Teams say they need to know one way or the other soon.

“I believe Stefano was targeting to tell us in mid-October,” said Haas team principal Ayao Komatsu in Azerbaijan. “So, we all know what the situation is.

“I believe that Imola is getting ready in case we have to do it. I think the challenges are, for instance, things like European motorhome structure, etcetera. All those people who look after them, they have a winter job, so we need to find alternative people to do that.

“But I’m sure we all, as a family, community, will make sure if we have to do that, that will happen. But hopefully, as a baseline, we can go to Qatar and Abu Dhabi. That would be really good.”

Drivers have pointed out the conditions could be very cold if the series races in Imola in December. However Audi team principal Mattia Binotto believes it would be no cooler than some other venues the series visits.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“The main challenges are more organisation and logistics,” he said. “I would think, from a technical point, often we may say wintertime and snow tyres, but at the end, as a matter of fact, the average temperature in Imola in that time of the year is hotter than Las Vegas.

“So I don’t think that’s a true concern. It’s more from the organisation and the logistics, really. And again, mid-October, hopefully we may do the right decision.”

Domenicali told the Financial Times the “decision is done” but also admitted “Imola is the place that eventually, in case of a force majeure before a certain date, would be ready to host it.”

Sports.title: Formula 1 announces it will race in Rwanda from “early 2030s” | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Formula 1 has announced it will return to race in Africa for the first time since 1993.

The series has agreed a 10-year deal to race in Rwanda, which has never previously held a round of the world championship. Unusually, no year for the inaugural race has been confirmed, with F1 saying only that it will “join the calendar in the early 2030s”.

A new circuit will be constructed in Bugesera, in the Eastern province of Rwanda. The track will be located 40 kilometres south of Rwanda’s capital Kigali, which hosted the FIA’s General Assembly and award ceremony in 2024.

F1 published an image of the planned RISE Motordrome circuit, which was created by Tilke Gmbh and Wurz Design, but gave no details of its specifications.

“Further details regarding the inaugural race date, circuit development milestones and race weekend plans will be announced in due course,” said F1.

According to Rwanda’s president Paul Kagame the race will be called the “Formula 1 African Grand Prix”.

F1 CEO Stefano Domenicali called the announcement “a landmark moment for Formula 1.”

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“With Rwanda joining the calendar from the next decade, our sport will race in every inhabited continent, bringing the world championship closer than ever to fans around the globe.”

F1 first raced in Africa in 1958, when Morocco’s Aib-Diab circuit held the final round of the season. However the series never returned to the northern African state.

The series found a longer-term home in South Africa, first at a track in East London, then at the popular Kyalami circuit near Johannesburg. South Africa held 23 grands prix, though the series faced growing criticism for holding events under the country’s racist apartheid regime, which led some teams to boycott the 1985 race.

Following a seven-year absence, F1 returned to a heavily revised Kyalami circuit for two races in the nineties.

By the time Rwanda hosts its first grand prix, up to 40 years may have passed since F1’s last race in Africa.

Sports.title: Carlos Adames Approval Leaves Meiirim Nursultanov Waiting
Sports.content:
Carlos Adames got the green light to take an interim bout before dealing with mandatory challenger Meiirim Nursultanov. The WBC approved a November 17 date above 160 pounds, but it includes a massive catch. If Adames loses, he loses his middleweight world title on the spot, even with the belt not officially on the line.

The WBC confirmed the ruling in an October 14 update. They left out the opponent, the venue, plus the exact weight limit. Because of that, nobody knows how tough this assignment will actually be.

Meiirim Nursultanov gets stuck waiting again. Holding the mandatory slot didn’t lock down his crack at the belt. Now he has to sit back, hoping Adames survives this detour so their scheduled clash can take place.

It puts Nursultanov in a weird spot. If Adames wins, Nursultanov still gets his shot at the active champion. If Adames stumbles, the title gets stripped, which leaves the top contender waiting on fresh orders for a vacant belt.

The WBC laid out clear terms. An Adames win routes him directly into the Nursultanov defense. Whoever walks away with the victory there has to face interim titlist Jesús Ramos Jr next.

There is a road map to clean up the division, but getting there takes three separate bouts. Every detour before the mandatory introduces the threat of an injury or an upset that blows up the entire schedule.

NEWS: Per sources, Carlos Adames’ @Zuffa_Boxing debut in a nontitle bout OK’d by the WBC is planned for November in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, where Zuffa is planning a show in November & one in December (obviously depends on status of the war & unrest in the region). #boxing — Dan Rafael (@DanRafael1) October 15, 2026

That vacant title rule also creates a bizarre setup for whoever steps into the ring on November 17. If the opponent beats the middleweight champ, Adames loses the belt, yet the winner walks away empty-handed without claiming it. Anyone signing that contract needs to realize what a victory actually delivers.

Adames lands the flexibility he wanted, while Nursultanov collects yet another promise about future dates. Until the promotion names a foe, nobody can tell if Adames is taking a dangerous test or just booking a tune-up above middleweight. Either way, Nursultanov stays on the sidelines waiting for his turn.

It sends a terrible message when a sanctioning body lets a champion put their mandatory obligations on ice just to chase an untitle bout above the weight class.

The whole point of a mandatory challenger is that you earn the number one spot through actual ring results, not politics. Nursultanov did the work, secured the position, and now he is forced to sit on the shelf watching the champion go hunt for bigger money elsewhere.

Nursultanov is not getting compensated while Adames takes this detour. Time away from the ring burns prime years, brings zero purse money, and creates ring rust. If Adames gets hurt on November 17, the layoff stretches out even longer. If Adames loses, Nursultanov does not even get the satisfaction or the profile boost of taking down the sitting champion. He gets stuck in a vacant title match that generates far less fanfare and a smaller check.

Sports.title: Sebastian Fundora Rules Out Saudi Arabia For Boots Fight
Sports.content:
Sebastian Fundora wants the winner of Jaron Ennis against Josh Kelly next, but the WBC junior middleweight champion insists Saudi Arabia will not host it. Fundora aims for spring 2027 to stage a unification bout, making it clear that facing Boots will not convince him to travel abroad to Riyadh.

That stance sets a firm condition on his future plans before his title defense against Ermal Hadribeaj on Saturday. Fundora expects Ennis to defeat Kelly, calling Boots the premier matchup at 154 pounds.

“I think the winner of Boots and Kelly should be the opponent for our next fight,” Fundora said to Ariel Helwani. “I think that’s early, early maybe springtime of next year, 2027.” Asked whether that reflected discussions or simply his preference, Fundora clarified: “That’s what I want. I think that’s what I’ll get as well.”

His preferred schedule remains a target rather than a signed contract, yet his refusal regarding Saudi Arabia sounded absolute.

“There’s a reason why I haven’t fought in Saudi Arabia,” Fundora said. “I wouldn’t feel comfortable, me being an American and everything like that.”

Asked directly if he would turn down an Ennis bout in the Gulf nation, Fundora confirmed he would walk away because that option feels unrealistic to him.

Securing an Ennis encounter would require common ground on location alongside purses. If promoters propose Saudi Arabia, Fundora makes it obvious that organizers must secure an alternate venue to get his signature.

He has not turned down an active offer to box Ennis. The scenario remains hypothetical right now, even while his desire to face the Ennis vs. Kelly victor is genuine.

Fundora must handle business against Hadribeaj first. Once Saturday concludes, his focus centers on collecting the remaining belts at 154 pounds in an arena he can accept. His stance puts him in a tricky spot financially. Crossing Riyadh off the list immediately shrinks the money pool, because nobody in the United States or the UK is writing those blank checks right now.

“My mother being a veteran and all the politics and that. It’s bigger than boxing. It’s way bigger than boxing,” said Fundora.

If PBC or another promoter has to finance an Ennis against Fundora unification on regular domestic pay-per-view, the numbers have to make sense organically, and that means significantly smaller paydays for both men.

Boots wants the belts, but he also wants to get paid like an elite fighter. If Fundora demands the bout take place in Vegas or Los Angeles, Ennis might look at the revenue split and decide the headache is not worth the discount, especially when other opportunities exist.

None of it matters if he looks past Saturday, either. Hadribeaj is not flying in just to collect a check and hand over the belt. If Fundora gets sloppy or gets caught while daydreaming about spring 2027, the whole discussion vanishes overnight. He will have priced himself out of an imaginary payday while holding empty hands.

Sports.title: Daniel Dubois’ Odd Preparations For His World Title Fight On Saturday
Sports.content:
As the WBO world title fight between Champion Daniel Dubois and Challenger and former WBO Champion Fabio Wardley in The O2 Arena in London, England approaches, it is interesting to observe how both fighters are preparing during fight week.

Both Dubois and Wardley are taking part in the usual media engagements this week to promote their fight. Other than that, Wardley is more low-key in his preparations. However, Dubois is attracting much more attention in the pre-fight buildup not just because he is the reigning WBO Champion, but also due to his rather strange pre-fight preparations.

In this regard, he went on a walkabout in Brixton, London, England, at the beginning of this week with his WBO belt. While it is admirable that Dubois is seen with people, and welcoming photos to be taken with him and well-wishers, he gives the impression that he is an all-conquering hero rather than a fighter preparing to defend his world title against a dangerous opponent. It would surely have been better for Dubois to delay his meet and greet until after he had actually beaten Wardley in Saturday’s fight.

Yet, this is not the first time that Daniel Dubois has done something peculiar in the week leading up to a world title fight. Who can forget his baffling presence at a party in the afternoon of his heavyweight world title clash against Oleksandr Usyk on 19 July last year at Wembley Stadium, London, England? On that occasion, some argued that Dubois allowed his focus to wander by attending this party, when it should have been squarely on making last-minute preparations for his fight against Usyk. They had a valid point, as Dubois ended up losing this fight by knockout in the 5th Round, and his IBF title in the process.

This opens up the debate about whether Dubois is taking Wardley’s challenge too lightly. In the buildup to Dubois v Wardley II, the WBO Champion has gone on record saying that beating Fabio Wardley on Saturday night will be easy. However, Wardley is right to say that if this is the case, Dubois would not have been knocked down twice in the early Rounds in their world title fight on 09 May.

Confidence is one thing. But complacency is a different thing altogether, and Dubois should be wary that he does not fall into this trap. To his credit, Wardley says that he has learned from the mistakes he made in his first fight with Dubois, and will correct them on Saturday. The Ipswich fighter is even honest enough to admit the punches, which earned him his two knockdowns of Dubois in the pair’s first fight, did not land completely accurately. Wardley argues that if they had done so, they would have caused more damage. Further, the video footage from this fight seems to bear this out.

We shall see on Saturday night whether Dubois has prepared correctly for the challenges Fabio Wardley brings. Will it be Repeat or Revenge? One thing for sure is that Daniel Dubois would be foolish to underestimate Wardley, who, like Dubois, has beaten convincingly a former World Champion. Wardley did so when he beat former WBO Champion Joseph Parker by TKO in the 11th Round on 25 October 2025 for the WBO interim heavyweight title.

Time will tell who will be the victor on Saturday night. It should be one helluva fight.

Romer Cherubim

Freelance journalist

Sports.title: Canelo Alvarez Needs Strong Finish To Saudi Contract
Sports.content:
Canelo Alvarez is eyeing a quick turnaround in February 2027 right after his October 31 meeting with Christian Mbilli. That timeline puts him on pace to wrap up his massive Saudi deal in just four months. How he performs down this final stretch will likely decide whether another giant contract follows.

“I want to fight quick, like in February,” Canelo said to Ring Magazine. “I have two fights left in Riyadh. So this one and another one.”

He wants February locked in, though nobody has named an opponent yet. Reports place his current four-fight package around $400 million, even if exact numbers stay private.

Canelo hasn’t said publicly that he wants an extension. Still, closing out the agreement forces the big question into the open: will the Saudis want to spend that kind of cash again?

His first two outings didn’t make a convincing pitch. William Scull left Canelo looking gun-shy. That bout really only existed to pick up the missing IBF belt rather than give fans an exciting matchup.

Against Terence Crawford, Canelo faded after round six. His sudden drop in punches looked like an aging fighter struggling with pace. Citing an injured elbow didn’t ease any doubts about his stamina.

Mbilli will push that gas tank immediately. Canelo needs an emphatic showing against a pressure fighter who won’t stop marching forward. Squeaking by with a disputed decision would damage his leverage, even if he leaves with his belts intact.

Assuming he clears Mbilli, February presents the next major hurdle. Hamzah Sheeraz brings strong British interest. David Benavidez or Osleys Iglesias would offer serious championship tests, though neither has received an official offer.

If Canelo dodges those challenges for an easier touch, the Saudis might start wondering what they are actually buying. Nobody knows how much control he holds over opponent selection anyway.

Dominating Mbilli before taking down elite competition would give Canelo real bargaining power. Another sluggish night marked by fading stamina could leave his next payday looking far smaller than what he is used to collecting.

If Riyadh Season is shelling out nine figures, they shouldn’t be subsidizing soft landings or vanity tours. Dropping rounds and gassing out against a 38-year-old blown-up welterweight like Crawford exposed the cliff Canelo is standing on. Pairing that with Scull in a dull performance showed zero return on entertainment value for the money spent.

Throwing him in with Benavidez or Ennis for the February finale would instantly force the issue.

Benavidez is the fight the public demanded for three years while Canelo priced himself out with absurd $150M to $200M demands. If Canelo wants another Saudi mega check, making him face the monster he avoided at 168 pounds is the only legitimate acid test left. He either proves he still possesses elite mettle or Benavidez completely takes the torch.

Jaron “Boots” Ennis would be pure tactical pressure. Boots would jump two weight classes, but his youth, hand speed, dynamic switch-hitting, and blistering volume would test Canelo’s fading stamina even worse than Crawford did down the stretch. Canelo cannot afford to stand flat-footed and rest against a guy throwing 70 punches a round.

IBF super middleweight champion Osleys Iglesias would be pure high risk, zero reward. The Cuban is a knockout artist who would likely batter this diminished version of Canelo, yet he doesn’t have the commercial profile to justify the Saudis burning their golden goose. There is no financial upside in letting an unknown derail the entire enterprise.

If Canelo rejects Benavidez or Ennis in February and insists on a soft touch like Edgar Berlanga 2 or John Ryder-level opposition, the Saudis have every reason to slam the checkbook shut. At this stage of his career, if he isn’t taking genuine risk into the ring, he isn’t worth the freight.

Sports.title: Anthony Olascuaga Faces Seven-Fight Challenger Yuberjen Martinez
Sports.content:
Anthony Olascuaga will defend his WBO flyweight title against seven-fight professional Yuberjen Martinez on November 14 at Dignity Health Sports Park in Carson, California. The unbeaten Colombian brings an Olympic silver medal and a perfect knockout record into a considerable jump in opposition.

Olascuaga (12-1, 9 KOs) makes his sixth title defense on the Diego Pacheco–Darius Fulghum undercard, with the event airing on DAZN and TNT Sports. The newly signed Matchroom fighter will also compete before his home Los Angeles crowd for the first time in his professional career.

Martinez (7-0, 7 KOs) gives the defense an interesting twist. His amateur pedigree separates him from the usual inexperienced challenger, but seven professional appearances leave plenty unanswered when the next opponent is an established world champion.

Stopping every opponent looks good on a poster. Doing it against the opposition Martinez has faced doesn’t establish that his power will have the same effect on Olascuaga. If the champion takes his punches and keeps coming, Martinez will need more than the finishing ability that has carried him through his professional fights.

That is where the scheduled 12-round distance becomes significant. Martinez’s Olympic success provides evidence of his boxing ability, but managing a world title fight requires decisions about pace, punch selection and energy that a short amateur contest cannot fully prepare him for.

Olascuaga has already been operating at championship level while Martinez has been building toward it. The challenger must show he can maintain his work when an experienced opponent forces him beyond the early success reflected in those seven stoppages.

The homecoming gives Olascuaga an opportunity to introduce himself to a local audience after defending his title in Japan. Matchroom gets a champion with Los Angeles roots on a card already headed by Pacheco.

Martinez gets the bigger opportunity: a chance to turn an accomplished amateur career and a brief professional run into a world championship. His medal makes him worth watching. This fight will tell us how far his professional boxing has progressed.

Sports.title: Naoya Inoue’s Team Rejects Robert Garcia’s Proposed Delay
Sports.content:
Naoya Inoue isn’t waiting around for anyone. His team officially shut the door on an April or May return, shutting down the timeline Robert Garcia floated for Jesse “Bam” Rodriguez.

The target remains February or March. If Rodriguez can’t make that window work, he misses his shot because Inoue plans to climb toward featherweight immediately.

Promoter Hideyuki Ohashi laid down the law on Wednesday. That stance creates real trouble for Garcia, especially since Rodriguez still lacks an official fight date for his bantamweight unification against Christian Medina.

“There won’t be April or May [next year],” Ohashi said to Hochi News.

Garcia floated spring dates for the matchup. Inoue previously announced he won’t delay his plans for Rodriguez, intending to begin his 126-pound preparations instead.

Meanwhile, Eddie Hearn claims an entirely different stance. The promoter hit back at Inoue by insisting their side welcomes the early schedule.

“Who’s waiting? You said you were fighting in February or March, right? We’re ready,” Hearn posted.

Hearn talks a big game, yet the Medina situation stays up in the air. Without a locked date for that unification, Rodriguez has no realistic timeline to fight Medina first, then jump up in weight for Inoue.

Should Hearn speak for the entire corner, the camps might sit closer to an agreement than Garcia suggested. If Garcia digs in on spring, Ohashi shut that idea down completely.

Inoue possesses every reason to stay active. Sticking around at 122 pounds strictly for Bam Rodriguez stalls his bid for a belt in a fifth weight class. His corner refuses to let historic goals depend on another fighter’s schedule. The fight can happen, but Hearn, Garcia, plus Rodriguez need internal aggreement first. Ohashi made Inoue’s stance crystal clear: the next ring walk will not shift into April or May for anyone.

Ohashi called their bluff immediately. Inoue holds every bit of leverage here. If Bam wants to cement real greatness, he steps up to the plate when the champion calls. Trying to slow-walk the fight only makes his team look hesitant, and Inoue is not going to put his featherweight goals on hold just to give Bam extra time to find his courage.

Sports.title: Fabio Wardley Questions Derek Chisora’s Retirement Advice
Sports.content:
Fabio Wardley has dismissed Derek Chisora’s prediction that the Daniel Dubois rematch could be his final fight, pointing to the veteran’s own refusal to retire. Chisora makes an easy target, although questioning his credibility won’t help Wardley avoid another punishing night against Dubois.

“This is specially funny coming from Derek who should have retired many a year ago and has still carried on,” Wardley told talkSPORT Boxing.

Wardley can dismiss Derek all day long. When the bell rings, he has to stop Dubois from handing him another brutal beating.

His punch power offers a real path to victory. Dubois gets hit plenty. Wardley doesn’t need to reinvent himself to land something concussive. Catching Dubois early could silence the retirement chatter immediately.

The real test arrives if Dubois weathers the early storm. Wardley can’t trade jabs with Dubois, who controls distance behind a heavier, straighter lead hand. Letting combinations fly creates openings, but staying in the pocket makes Fabio an easy target unless he exits instantly.

Wardley mentioned his camp didn’t add special safety measures, choosing to ramp up workout tempo instead. That comment says nothing about tactical adjustments, since he addressed injury prevention rather than fight strategy.

Training harder in the gym won’t erase the danger Dubois brings. Better stamina might keep Wardley active late, but it won’t stop a stiff jab cracking his nose. It won’t deflect a hard right hand when he steps inside, either.

Chisora lecturing anyone on when to hang up the gloves is rich considering his own track record. Since knocking out Carlos Takam eight years ago, his record has been a parade of beatings at the elite level, interrupted only by narrow decisions over fading names like Kubrat Pulev, Gerald Washington, and domestic gatekeepers.

When Tyson Fury was using him as target practice in their third meeting while the referee practically begged Chisora’s corner to stop it, nobody thought, ‘Now there goes a man with sound judgment on ring longevity.’

Sports.title: Filip Hrgovic Calls Frank Sanchez Defense a ‘Maybe’
Sports.content:
Filip Hrgovic sees himself competing in the heavyweight division for another five years. His recent comments regarding mandatory challenger Frank Sanchez, however, spark an immediate debate over his willingness to face the Cuban next.

Talking through potential matchups with reporters, Hrgovic pointed toward Agit Kabayel and the winner of Daniel Dubois versus Fabio Wardley 2 before tossing in, “or maybe my mandatory,” according to The Ring.

That kind of phrasing is as transparent as glass. When a newly crowned champion starts referring to his official number one contender as “maybe my mandatory,” that is not a slip of the tongue. That is pure preservation instinct kicking in. Unfiltered remarks often expose a fighter’s true intentions faster than any scripted press release.

Hrgovic has not officially declined the fight, but brushing off his primary obligation as “maybe my mandatory” sounds suspiciously evasive. He understands how sanctioning bodies operate. Treating a mandated defense as an open question makes it look like he hopes the requirement simply disappears.

Hrgovic knows exactly what he survived against Moses Itauma. He got battered pillar to post, lost virtually every single second of the first eight rounds, and only walked away with the belt because a 21-year-old blew his entire engine looking for an early highlight reel. You cannot build a five-year reign on the hope that every opponent will gas out after eight rounds of teeing off on your chin.

Frank Sanchez represents the worst possible stylistic matchup for Hrgovic right now. The Cuban is powerful, disciplined, skilled, and does not sell out for wild early knockouts. He will not punch himself into exhaustion. Sanchez would force Hrgovic to actually box, lead, cut off the ring, and win rounds on skill and volume, things Hrgovic has struggled with whenever he steps up in class.

“I think I have a lot of fights left,” Hrgovic explained. “And I want to unify. I don’t know the exact number of fights, but I think I can be here for five more years.”

Planning a half-decade run at the top is bold talk for someone whose grip on the belt remains so fragile.

Chasing unification against the Dubois-Wardley winner certainly promises a richer payday. Neither option represents a walk in the park, though. Dubois previously stopped the Croatian, and Wardley possesses the raw power to scramble anyone’s night.

The sport is supposed to run on the mandatory system, forcing champions to defend against the rightful top contenders. When a guy wins a belt by the skin of his teeth and immediately starts scheming ways to bypass the division’s trickiest puzzle, it tells you everything you need to know about how confident his team really is in his longevity. If he actually fights Sanchez next, it will only be because the sanctioning body backed him into a corner with no exit.

Ghana News.title: Total expenditure as of July 2026 amounted to GH¢147.07bn, 16% below target – BoG
Ghana News.content:
Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson

The government spent less in the first seven months of 2026, as Total Expenditures and Net Lending totaled GH¢147.077 billion in July 2026.

This was below the target of GH¢175.931.9 million by 16.4%.

According to the July 2026 Monetary Policy Report, Compensation of Employees amounted to GH¢50.553 billion, lower than the target of GH¢52.943 billion.

This outturn was below its target by 4.5% but recorded a 12.6% year-on-year growth.

The compensation budget of government employees constituted 35.2% of domestic revenue mobilised during the period under review.

The Use of Goods and Services totalled GH¢5.482 billion, lower than the expected target of GH¢7.897 billion. This outturn represented a year-on-year growth of 63.4%.

Total Interest Payments amounted to GH¢25.171 billion against the budget target of GH¢34.117 billion and 12.3% below the outturn of GH¢28.686 billion recorded in the corresponding period of 2025.

The reduction in interest payments was mainly on account of lower domestic interest payments as well as front loading of some Eurobond payments made at the end of 2025 which were originally programmed for 2026.

Grants to Other Government Units amounted to GH¢30.611 billion, lower than the target of GH¢35.866 billion. This outturn represented a year-on-year decline of 1.6%.

The Capital Expenditure amounted to GH¢24.228 billion (1.5% of Gross Domestic Product). This is lower than the programmed target by 25%.

This outturn represented a year-on-year growth of 157.9%.

Other Expenditure amounted to GH¢9.283 billion, 13.4% below the target. This outturn compared with GH¢8,107 billion recorded in the corresponding period of 2025.

Factors Behind Expenditure Performance

The report said the improved macroeconomic conditions had a positive knock-on impact on total interest payments.

Again, the relative stability of the Ghana cedi also reduced external interest costs.

The external interest payments also fell due to the front-loading of some payments made at the end of 2025 that were originally programmed for 2026.

In addition, the government benefited from reduced Eurobond debt servicing and concessional refinancing arrangements.

The reduction in goods and services stemmed from the containment of administrative spending, demonstrating the government’s continued focus on efficiency and value-for money across MDAs.

“Other expenditure” also fell, reflecting continued progress in rationalising energy-related obligations and improving efficiency in sector financing.

The fall in capital expenditure was due to the operationalisation of the commitment authorisation policy as stipulated in the PFM Act where payments for completed projects are only made on submission of invoices by contractors.

Ghana News.title: Total revenue & grants stood at GH¢144.5bn in July 2026, slightly below target – BoG
Ghana News.content:
The Total Revenue and Grants in the first seven months of 2026 amounted to GH¢144.571 billion, about 9.1% of Gross Domestic Product (GDP).

This was slightly lower than the target of GH¢144.951 billion (9.1% of GDP).

According to the September 2026 Monetary Policy Report, domestic revenue totalled GH¢143.522 billion (9.0% of GDP) in July 2026, below the target of GH¢143,630.9 million (9.0% of GDP).

The report alluded that the revenue outcomes reflected marginal underperformance of tax revenue, oil revenue, as well as grants.

Tax Revenue (comprising taxes on income and property, taxes on domestic goods and services, international trade taxes, and oil and gas related taxes) amounted to GH¢120.008 billion (7.5% of GDP), lower than the target of GH¢121.033 billion (7.6% of GDP).

This represented a negative deviation of 0.8% from the target.

Non-Tax Revenue totalled GH¢14.562 billion, below the target of GH¢16.590 billion by 12.2%.

Compared with the outturn for 2025, this translates into a year-on-year growth of 1.0%.

According to the report, this performance was mainly due to lower-than-programmed Dividend/Interest and Profits from Oil (CAPI) as well as the Yield from Capping Policy for the collection period.

Oil Revenue amounted to GH¢6.290 billion, lower than the target of GH¢9.064 billion by 30.6%.

This tax type also recorded a year-on-year growth of 6.3%.

Other Revenue amounted to GH¢8.950 billion, above its target of GH¢5.174 billion, representing an overperformance by 73%. This outturn was 117.9% above GH¢4.106 billion collected in the corresponding period of 2025.

Grants received for January-July 2026 totalled GH¢1.049 billion, a shortfall of 20.5% from the programmed target of GH¢1.320 billion. This outturn was also higher than GH¢452.7 million received in the corresponding period of 2025, translating into a year-on-year growth of 131.8%.

Drivers of Revenue Performance

Corporate income tax was 21.7% above target, which could be attributed to higher payments by major mining companies due to the increase in the average price of gold and growth in revenue from the banking sector.

According to the report, there was also an increase in mineral royalties, which was due to the increase in the average gold price above the US$4,000 per fine ounce threshold, triggering the application of a higher mineral royalty rate for taxpayers.

However, the expected revenue from the import sector fell short of target due to undershooting of CIF targets for the period.

Also, petroleum sector revenue was below target.

There was a shortfall in grants, which reflected in delays in project disbursements from development partners.

Ghana News.title: Ghana Sports Fund urges sports federations to submit credible proposals and measurable targets
Ghana News.content:
The Administrator of the Ghana Sports Fund, Dr David Kofi Wuaku, has challenged national sports federations to take greater responsibility for their development plans and demonstrate how proposed funding will improve athlete development and sporting performance.

He said sustainable sports development would require federations to identify their most pressing needs, prepare credible proposals and establish realistic budgets and measurable targets.

Addressing representatives of national sports federations in Accra, Dr Wuaku called for stronger strategic planning, effective administration and measurable performance across the sporting sector.

“I challenge every federation to take ownership of its development agenda. Identify your priority needs, prepare credible proposals, establish realistic budgets and measurable targets, and demonstrate how the support you seek will improve athlete development and sporting performance,” he said.

Dr Wuaku explained that the Ghana Sports Fund was being developed to provide a sustainable financing framework for sports, but said its effectiveness would depend partly on the readiness and cooperation of the federations.

He urged them to strengthen governance systems, improve financial reporting and develop clear plans for talent identification, athlete preparation and competition.

He also encouraged federations to explore partnerships with corporate Ghana, private investors and development partners, stressing that reliance on funding requests alone would not provide a sustainable basis for sports development.

According to him, federations must demonstrate what they intend to achieve, how proposed interventions would be implemented and how their impact would be measured.

The Ghana Sports Fund Act, 2025 (Act 1159), identifies federations and associations in good standing with the National Sports Authority as eligible beneficiaries of the Fund.

However, Dr Wuaku clarified that eligibility does not automatically entitle a federation to financial support.

Applications must meet the applicable requirements and pass through the relevant assessment and approval processes before funding can be granted.

The engagement is intended to help the Fund better understand the operational, technical and financial challenges confronting different sporting disciplines.

It is also expected to encourage federations to develop structured proposals that can guide future funding priorities.

Dr Wuaku said the Fund was committed to establishing a credible and transparent financing system, while emphasising that federations would need to demonstrate readiness, sound planning and accountability.

Ghana News.title: Sally Rooney books withdrawn in UK over Palestine Action support
Ghana News.content:
Normal People author Sally Rooney has said her novels will no longer be supplied to booksellers in the UK as a result of her support for Palestine Action.

The Irish novelist said last year she intended to carry on using her royalties to support the group, which is a proscribed terrorist organisation in the UK.

In a statement to BBC News, Rooney said that further publication of her work could constitute a "serious criminal offence", so she had agreed with her publisher, Faber, not to continue supplying her books in the UK.

"I have made every effort to be honest with the public about my beliefs and intentions, and I am wholly prepared to accept the consequences," she said.

Ebook editions have already been removed from sale in the UK, although many bookshops still have existing stock of physical copies.

Waterstones confirmed to the BBC that Faber had advised there were no restrictions on booksellers keeping their current copies on the shelves.

Rooney has sold more than six million books globally, including 2.3 million in the UK, according to NielsenIQ BookData.

Normal People was released in 2018 and turned into a hit TV series two years later, effectively launching the acting careers of Paul Mescal and Daisy Edgar-Jones.

Rooney's other novels are Intermezzo, Conversations With Friends and Beautiful World, Where Are You.

Publisher Faber told BBC News: "Current legislation in the UK has led to circumstances where Faber cannot pass on UK earnings to Sally Rooney for her work.

"To sell a writer's work and not be able to pass on earnings is an unconscionable situation for a publisher.

"As such, and in full agreement with Sally, we have taken the decision that we can no longer supply her works in the UK in any format."

Faber added: "We remain the proud publisher of her remarkable body of work, which we will continue to sell in other territories."

Rooney's four novels, including her most recent, Intermezzo, will be removed from sale in the UK

The UK government proscribed Palestine Action as a terrorist organisation in 2025, saying it had a "long history" of criminal damage.

The group's activities have included targeting arms companies linked to Israel's war in Gaza.

In her statement on Wednesday, Rooney said: "In July 2025, the direct-action protest group Palestine Action was proscribed as a terrorist organisation in the UK.

"The following month, I wrote an opinion piece expressing my intention to go on supporting Palestine Action, which is not a proscribed or otherwise prohibited group here in the Republic of Ireland."

In her article last August in the Irish Times, Rooney said she would continue using proceeds from her work to support the group despite that being an offence in the UK, and cancelled a UK trip to pick up an award over fears she would be arrested.

On Wednesday, Rooney continued: "As a result, the fulfilment of contracts to publish my work in the UK could now constitute a serious criminal offence.

"After a process of consultation and deliberation, and with my full agreement, my publisher Faber has therefore determined that it can no longer supply my work within the UK."

Palestine Action co-founder Huda Ammori said Rooney had taken "a brave and principled stand from the moment plans to ban Palestine Action were announced".

Ammori said the author's work being withdrawn marked "a new low in the escalating assault on free speech caused by the proscription of Palestine Action".

More than 3,700 people are believed to have been arrested in the UK over alleged support of Palestine Action.

About 2,500 have been charged, although none have gone to trial as a legal challenge to the proscription continues and will be heard by the Supreme Court next month.

Ghana News.title: Musk says US government may be behind slowdown of Ukraine drone speeds
Ghana News.content:
Elon Musk, Chief Executive Officer of SpaceX and Tesla and owner of X, formerly known as Twitter, attends the Viva Technology conference dedicated to innovation and startups at the Porte de Versailles exhibition centre in Paris, France, June 16, 2023. REUTERS/Gonzalo Fuentes/File Photo Acquire Licensing Rights

Elon Musk has suggested that the US government may be behind restrictions on the speed at which some of Ukraine's weapons can travel and stay connected to SpaceX's Starlink internet network.

Starlink is a vital tool allowing Kyiv to guide drones to Russian targets and also protect its own skies, but on Tuesday night Ukraine said unexpected new speed limits were disrupting its battlefield missions.

An adviser to President Volodymyr Zelensky said he believed the restrictions were not a coincidence and were related to the latest strains between Kyiv and Washington.

Musk said that Starshield, the military-grade sister service to Starlink, is controlled by the US government, and "any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately [the US president]".

Musk - writing on X - had been responding to pleas from Ukrainian officials to restore connectivity, including from Zelensky who told UK media: "I hope that it's a mistake, maybe [a] huge technical problem. I don't know, but we are asking to... switch [it] on."

Starlink, which is owned by Musk's SpaceX, restricted speed limits on Tuesday night to 100mph (160km/h), meaning any weapons that travelled faster than that lost connectivity to the network.

It had been partially restored by Wednesday evening, Ukraine's former defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov said.

"Removing Starshield's speed limit entirely is now critical for Ukraine's defense," he wrote on X, thanking Elon Musk and asking for his "continued support".

About an hour later, Musk replied to that post, defending his company's involvement.

"Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the US government. Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS," he wrote.

Musk added that Starlink is for "civilian or defensive activities and cannot be used for offensive military action, as doing so would be inappropriate for a commercial company".

The US government has not commented.

While both companies are owned by Musk's SpaceX, Starlink is a civilian service that uses satellites in low Earth orbit to provide internet access, particularly in remote areas, while Starshield is designed for government and military use.

The restrictions on Tuesday night came as Russia launched deadly attacks against Ukraine that killed several people in Kyiv, officials said, and hit communications and energy facilities used by Ukraine's military.

Zelensky said it was "one of the largest attacks" from Russia, and while "a significant part of the drones were shot down" there were "also hits".

At least 600,000 people across Ukraine were left without electricity, and residents said they received no warning of incoming drones before they hit.

"It is clear that this action cannot be a coincidence and is related to the current political situation," Zelensky's adviser Serhiy Beskrestnov wrote on Telegram on Wednesday morning.

US President Donald Trump has grown increasingly frustrated towards Ukraine as it continues to strike Russian energy facilities.

Zelensky has said that the US threatened to restrict intelligence sharing if he did not sign up to Trump's energy ceasefire, but on Tuesday, Trump denied this.

Speaking during a visit to London on Wednesday, Zelensky agreed that he had felt betrayed after the US made a deal with Russia to import 300,000 tonnes of its diesel.

"Really yes... but it's a little bit more complicated than just my emotions or my feelings," Zelensky said, when asked by UK journalist Piers Morgan if he felt betrayed.

During his one-day visit, Zelensky was greeted with a hug by UK PM Andy Burnham at Downing Street and held an audience with King Charles.

Ahead of the president's arrival, No 10 announced it would speed up delivery of lightweight multirole missiles to Ukraine, which have been used to bring down Russian drones.

"We are behind you and that will not change," Burnham told Zelensky.

Ghana News.title: Picking Chief Justices nearing retirement could give Mahama immense power – Bentil
Ghana News.content:
Lawyer and Vice President of Imani Africa, Kofi Bentil

Lawyer and Vice-President of IMANI Africa, Kofi Bentil, says appointing Chief Justices close to retirement could give President John Mahama immense power by allowing him to choose successive heads of the judiciary.

Speaking on JoyNews’ PM Express on Wednesday, he said the remaining years of potential appointees could become a political consideration.

“If the president wants to wrestle power, he will go the route of picking people with short times to go,” he said.

Mr Bentil stressed that this was a possibility, rather than a claim about the President’s intentions.

“I said, if he wants, okay. The reason is simple. It will give him immense power.”

He explained that choosing judges with short periods left in office could allow President Mahama to appoint at least two Chief Justices before leaving office.

The succession question comes as Chief Justice Paul Baffoe-Bonnie approaches retirement later this year. His departure will require another appointment to lead the judiciary.

Mr Bentil said competence remained essential. But he argued that it was unlikely to be the only consideration when choosing a Chief Justice.

“Competence is always important, but even in corporate life, above a certain level, the boss will pick somebody with sufficient competence and great loyalty.”

He said the judges under consideration were qualified for the position. “There can be no mistake, regardless of who is picked. They are all really fit.”

The decisive issue, he suggested, could be the President’s comfort with a candidate.

“I think that to the extent that it is the president who picks, he will pick a choice that is comfortable for him.”

For Bentil, however, the appointment should help rebuild public confidence following the turmoil surrounding the judiciary.

“I think the best thing would be someone who projects confidence in the judiciary.”

He acknowledged that no candidate would satisfy everyone. Still, he wanted a choice that could command broad acceptance among judges, lawyers and the public.

Despite his concerns about political considerations, Mr Kofi Bentil expressed confidence in the available candidates.

“I think ultimately the president will make a good choice because fortunately we have very good people over there, but he will make the choice.”

Ghana News.title: Netflix to shed 1,000 jobs in steepest cuts since 2022
Ghana News.content:
Netflix has said it will cut 1,000 jobs globally as the streaming giant faces competition from rivals.

The cuts - the steepest since 2022 - will mainly affect its human resources, legal, product and technology teams and equate to around 6% of its total workforce.

Last month, Netflix's co-chief executive, Ted Sarandos, told the Bloomberg Screentime summit that the company was "not growing as fast as I want us to".

The streaming industry is going through a period of consolidation following Paramount's $110bn (£83.6bn) merger with Warner Bros., the owner of HBO, while free platforms such as YouTube and TikTok continue to attract viewers.

In an email to staff, Sarandos and co-chief executive Greg Peters said Netflix would "continue to invest aggressively in high-impact areas to improve our service and further drive growth and innovation".

Netflix had come close to striking its own deal with Warner Bros., but was ultimately outbid by Paramount.

Commenting on the "organisational changes", Sarandos and Peters said: "Our mission - to entertain the world - is ambitious, and delivering on it requires us to be disciplined about where we prioritise our people and resources."

Managers will tell employees whether their job has been cut "soon".

TV series Below, starring Josh Hartnett, is one of Netflix's most popular shows

The email added that the firm was on track to meet its financial forecasts. The streaming service is due to report its latest results on 20 October.

Investors have been weighing up user engagement - the amount of time customers spend on Netflix - as it competes with platforms such as YouTube and TikTok.

The firm has continued to commission shows - its most popular at the moment is "Below", an underwater mystery series.

It has also been attempting to expand its business, including gaming and allowing adverts to play before and during shows and films.

However, "they haven't been able to find another line of major revenue," said Ross Benes, senior analyst at eMarketer.

He added that the company remains reliant on a subscription business that could be approaching a plateau.

"Eventually, because they're nearing a ceiling with that, they'll need another revenue stream to diversify, and that's where it's been more of a struggle," he said.

The last major round of redundancies at Netflix was in 2022, when it cut about 450 jobs after losing subscribers for the first time in more than a decade.

Ghana News.title: Burnham had two hospitality dinners with Man City chairman, deleted records show
Ghana News.content:
Man City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak (left) chats to Andy Burnham in 2019 at the Etihad Stadium, when he was mayor of Greater Manchester

Andy Burnham had two hospitality dinners with Manchester City football club's chairman while mayor of Greater Manchester, it has emerged.

The PM dined with Khaldoon Al Mubarak at matches in 2017 and 2018 - but this was not detailed in a statement on Monday by the Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA) about his meetings with the club.

Burnham has been under pressure to clarify his previous discussions with Man City since the club was found guilty of having "systematically" broken Premier League rules, which it will appeal.

The PM, who was mayor until June, sparked widespread controversy when he said last month that he would be "really concerned" if the club's owners sold up now.

On Monday, the GMCA released a statement about Burnham's meetings with Man City during his nearly decade-long tenure as mayor of the region.

The statement said he had a formal meeting with Al Mubarak in October 2021 at the UK Government's Global Investment Summit, arranged by the Department for International Trade; and that he met the club chairman "informally in the stands" at a testimonial match in 2019 for former player Vincent Kompany.

It also said that "in his capacity as mayor, he was a guest of Manchester City at home matches on a small number of occasions".

But the statement did not specify that this referred to two hospitality dinners he had with the Manchester City chairman at separate matches.

A previous GMCA register of declarations for Burnham, seen by the BBC, detailed a "dinner with [then-Manchester City Council leader] Richard Leese and Chair of Man City" for an Everton match at the Etihad stadium in August 2017, valued at £300 for hospitality.

Below is another entry for "dinner with the Chairman at the Man City/Man Utd derby at the Etihad" in April 2018, valued at approximately £699.

Burnham previously declared those dinners, alongside a £150 pair of tickets to see Ed Sheeran perform at the stadium in May 2018.

But the register of declarations has since been deleted from the GMCA website, as first reported by The Sun. The BBC understands that it is the authority's policy to publish only entries from the current mayoral term.

BBC News has asked GMCA for more details about this policy - given its website has entries dating back to 2022, despite the current mayoral term beginning in 2024.

Downing Street has defended the two dinners with Man City's chairman, saying this was hospitality received at home games, which had been declared, rather than separate meetings with the club chairman.

But political pressure on Burnham to be clearer about any former discussions with Man City is continuing to mount.

Tory shadow sports minister Louie French said: "Andy Burnham promised the country and House of Commons full transparency on his dealings with Manchester City.

"This was essential after his inappropriate intervention into football."

And Reform UK's Robert Jenrick said "this saga stinks" as he accused Burnham of having apparently "concealed his extensive links to Man City's owners".

Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch has demanded for several days that No 10 release all details of meetings between the prime minister and senior figures at the club.

Burnham told the Rest Is Politics podcast last week he was "happy" to do this and would "quite clearly put out there everything that I have done working with them in my previous role as Mayor of Greater Manchester".

"None of it is recent, actually, in terms of the meetings I had. I only had one significant meeting, actually, and that was in 2021."

Asked at Prime Minister's Questions on Wednesday whether anyone at the club had raised the charges they were facing with him or his team, Burnham said: "They did not raise those issues with me."

With the PM continuing to face pressure on the issue, he told MPs he was happy for "everything to be set out in full", referring to the GMCA's statement as "a full statement of my key dealings with the owners of Manchester City Football Club".

When asked by reporters why the statement did not refer to the two dinners, and what the difference is between "everything" and "key dealings", the PM's press secretary referred back to the GMCA statement.

The list of meetings, which was published by the GMCA on Monday, did not include detail on what was discussed. The BBC has asked GMCA why the two dinners were not specifically mentioned.

In September Man City - which has dominated the top flight of English football for years - was found guilty by an independent commission of breaching Premier League financial regulations.

The commission found City had broken rules over a nine-year period between 2009 and 2018 by creating "sham" contracts with commercial partners to secretly funnel more than £830m into their football operations.

Sanctions are yet to be announced and City, which denies any wrongdoing, has lodged an appeal against the verdict.

Earlier this month, Sir Richard Leese - who was head of Manchester City Council for 25 years until 2021 - defended a decade-old deal between the council and Man City owners Abu Dhabi United Group (ADUG).

Under the partnership between the authority and the company, which is linked to the United Arab Emirates royal family, land was leased to ADUG at "below comparable rates", according to a University of Sheffield report.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
