World.title: UCL: Real Madrid stage dramatic comeback to beat Roma 4-3
World.content:
Real Madrid scored three late goals to overturn a two-goal deficit and secure a dramatic 4-3 victory over Roma in the UEFA Champions League on Jose Mourinho’s return to the Stadio Olimpico.

Madrid appeared destined for defeat after Roma took a 3-1 lead in the 83rd minute, but substitutes Carlos Espi and Endrick inspired a stunning comeback before Antonio Rudiger struck the decisive goal in the 90th minute.

The victory extended Real Madrid’s perfect start to their Champions League campaign, having won both matches, while Roma were left with one point from their opening two games.

Mourinho, who previously led Roma to the Europa Conference League title in 2021-22 and the Europa League final the following season, received a warm reception from the home supporters, who displayed banners celebrating his time at the Italian club.

Roma made a strong start and took the lead in the 20th minute when Marten de Roon fired a first-time effort from the edge of the box after being set up by Matias Soule.

Real Madrid responded five minutes later through Kylian Mbappe, whose effort took a deflection off Gianluca Mancini before looping over goalkeeper Pierluigi Gollini.

The goal was Mbappe’s 72nd in the Champions League, moving him ahead of Real Madrid legend Raul, who finished his career in the competition with 71 goals. The appearance also marked the French forward’s 100th match in the tournament.

Roma regained control after the break, with Donyell Malen scoring twice in a six-minute spell to put the hosts in a commanding position.

Malen made it 2-1 after capitalising on a mistake by Vinicius Junior, whose attempted flick gave away possession. The striker’s shot took a deflection off Real Madrid captain Federico Valverde before finding the net.

The Dutch forward struck again soon afterwards, finishing calmly to extend Roma’s advantage to 3-1. Although the goal was initially ruled out for offside, a video assistant referee review confirmed that Valverde had kept Malen onside.

Roma manager Gian Piero Gasperini introduced several defensive substitutes as he attempted to protect the lead, but Real Madrid’s late attacking changes proved decisive.

Espi pulled one back five minutes after coming on, converting the rebound after Gollini had parried Endrick’s header.

Endrick then levelled the contest by heading home from an Arda Guler corner, leaving Roma struggling to contain Madrid’s set-piece threat.

The visitors completed the turnaround in the 90th minute when Rudiger volleyed home from close range following another Guler delivery to seal a remarkable 4-3 win.

The result provides a boost for Real Madrid as they continue their Champions League campaign, while Roma will need to improve after failing to hold on to their advantage on home soil.

World.title: ‘Expanded APC Campaign Council a confession of fear’ — Atiku
World.content:
Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has described the expanded presidential campaign council of the All Progressives Congress (APC) as a “confession of fear”, accusing President Bola Tinubu of prioritising political alliances over Nigeria’s economic hardship and insecurity.

Atiku, the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), said the expansion of the council for the 2027 general election reflected the president’s concern about his political standing rather than the challenges facing Nigerians.

In a statement issued on Wednesday by Phrank Shaibu, director of strategic communication of the ADC presidential campaign council, Atiku argued that the inclusion of more political figures would not address hunger, violence, kidnappings and the rising cost of living.

“Only a man afraid of his record would think he could bury it under hundreds of names,” the statement reads.

“Tinubu can gather every governor, minister and political defector in Nigeria. None of them can erase the hunger in people’s homes, bring back those killed by violence or free Nigerians still held captive. Their families are waiting for answers, not another campaign list.”

The APC initially released its presidential campaign council list on August 22, naming Abdulaziz Yari, former governor of Zamfara State, as director-general. The expanded council includes Nyesom Wike, minister of the Federal Capital Territory;

Ademola Adeleke, governor of Osun State; and Chukwuma Soludo, governor of Anambra State.

Atiku also accused Tinubu of maintaining an extensive political structure while Nigerians grapple with the consequences of rising prices and declining purchasing power.

“Tinubu has room for an army of ministers and a stadium full of campaign officials, but no room in his plans for Nigerians crushed by the cost of living. He feeds his political machine and tells hungry families to sacrifice,” he said.

The former vice-president maintained that adding more names to the campaign council would not change Nigerians’ experiences under the current administration.

He also faulted the decision to inaugurate the APC campaign council at the Presidential Villa in Abuja, describing the venue as public property that should not be used for partisan political activities.

“The Presidential Villa belongs to the Nigerian people. It is not a campaign venue or the private property of any political party. Using it for an APC political event is a gross breach of public trust and a troubling abuse of public office,” he said.

Questioning the choice of venue, Atiku argued that Abuja had sufficient alternative locations for the event.

“Abuja has no shortage of halls and public spaces large enough to host a campaign gathering. Why, then, did Bola Tinubu choose to inaugurate his campaign council at night, behind the gates of the Presidential Villa?” he asked.

He said the decision raised questions about the president’s confidence in his performance, adding that Nigerians should assess his

administration based on their experiences.

“Nigerians may draw their own conclusions. But a president confident in his record should be willing to face the public in daylight and ask for another mandate,” he said.

Atiku further described the expanded council as an attempt to shield Tinubu from public criticism by recruiting more political figures, including members of other parties.

“When the first list drew criticism, Tinubu had a chance to show that he understood the country’s anger. Instead, he returned with an even longer list, reaching into other parties for more names. He is collecting politicians like shields against public judgment,” he said.

The ADC presidential candidate also cited a claim that 17.9 million more Nigerians were living in multidimensional poverty, linking the figure to the economic and security challenges confronting the country.

He argued that the enlarged campaign structure would do little to make food affordable or improve the purchasing power of workers and other citizens.

“No campaign council, however crowded, can make food affordable, restore a worker’s purchasing power or explain why the sacrifices demanded of ordinary Nigerians never seem to reach Tinubu’s own political circle,” he said.

Atiku said the ADC had assembled its own campaign team to offer Nigerians an alternative, insisting that voters would ultimately judge the president by their living conditions rather than the number of political figures backing his re-election bid.

“On January 16, the ballot will contain no column for the size of a campaign council. Nigerians will judge Tinubu by the lives they have lived under his government,” he added.

World.title: PSG beat Manchester City 4-2 away in Champions League
World.content:
Manchester City’s Norwegian striker #09 Erling Haaland (2R) misses with this header during the UEFA Champions League, league phase football match between Manchester City and Paris Saint Germain at the Etihad Stadium in Manchester, north west England, on October 14, 2026. (Photo by Oli SCARFF / AFP)

Reigning champions Paris Saint-Germain staved off a second-half comeback to win 4-2 away to Manchester City in their Champions League showdown on Wednesday.

PSG were 3-0 up in the first half with goals by Desire Doue, Ousmane Dembele and Vitinha, but Erling Haaland scored twice after the break for City. Maghnes Akliouche got PSG’s fourth before Ferran Torres had a late penalty saved.

World.title: 2027: You’re tired, weak, go home – Adebayo tells Tinubu
World.content:
Presidential candidate of the Social Democratic Party, SDP, for 2027, Prince Adewole Adebayo, has urged President Bola Tinubu to go home and let Nigeria breathe.

Adebayo said this in a statement, in Abuja, on Wednesday.

He was responding to the President’s plan to excuse himself from the rigors of physical campaigns in some states ahead of the presidential polls.

Tinubu spoke at the inauguration of the APC Presidential Campaign Council in Abuja, where he urged members to take the party’s message to Nigerians across the states and local government areas while he continues to attend to matters of governance.

In response, Adebayo said if Tinubu is too tired to campaign, he is too weak to govern.

In a statement signed by his Presidential Campaign’s Chief Communications Adviser, Comrade Mark Adebayo, the SDP candidate described Tinubu as a “president in absentia” at a time Nigeria needs hands-on leadership.

Adebayo said, “Nigeria is too complex, too dynamic, and currently too distressed to be governed by remote control.”

He cited what he called repeated instances of the President governing from a distance, including prolonged medical vacations disguised as working visits, absence during national emergencies and reliance on proxies to announce state policies.

The SDP candidate further said, “We have seen repeated instances where the President is visibly missing when the country needs reassurance.

“From unannounced foreign trips during critical economic decisions to his complete silence during widespread regional protests, he has consistently acted like a president in absentia. If you are too tired to campaign, you are too weak to govern.”

Adebayo alleged that the decision to stay off the campaign trail was not about strategy but fear.

“The excuse of bowing out of the 2027 campaign is a cowardly smokescreen. The truth is that the President is terrified of the Nigerian people,” he argued.

According to him, the administration’s economic policies – fuel subsidy removal fallout, skyrocketing inflation and currency instability -have made the President unpopular.

“He knows the pain his bad policies have inflicted on families. He is hiding because he cannot face public anger, and he knows any appearance on a campaign trail will be met with collective booing of a betrayed populace.”

Adebayo also said, “It is time to face reality: step aside, go home, and let this country breathe.”

He called on the administration to prioritise national interest over political survival and be transparent about the President’s capacity to lead for the remainder of his term.

World.title: Nigerians better off under Tinubu, APC spokesman insists
World.content:
Tinubu

By Dickson Omobola

National Publicity Secretary of the All Progressives Congress, APC, Felix Muoka, has insisted that Nigeria and Nigerians are better off than ever before, saying the party will win the 2027 presidential election based on its positive records.

Muoka said the APC was working hard to secure voters’ support, adding that the party would not take Nigerians’ votes for granted.

Speaking on Politics Today, a Channels Television programme, Thursday, he said the party’s preparations and campaign efforts were aimed at securing as many votes as possible in the next general elections.

He said: “Qualitatively speaking, our country is better. Nigerians are better today than they have ever been. Is there a country that has transited from this depressed economy, like we have had for decades, to that level of prosperity that didn’t go through these stages?

“Nigerians also understand that. So what the president has done is to give this country a fighting chance, not just at recovery, but at building the prospects for sustainable prosperity.”

On the inauguration of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, he said: “What you saw today and what we’ve been up to is really taking ourselves seriously. If we thought this was all said and done, we wouldn’t put in this level of energy and work in an effort to really get to the last vote within the electorate. We are not taking this for granted. We’re taking it very seriously. I’m sure that if our party was docile and we were doing nothing to campaign or put out our information, you would also bring me here to say that we had been very docile. We’re a political party.

“We are a party for a reason. We are in this to compete with other political parties and to win the support of Nigerians. Since 2023, there’s a reason that our party has been very successful. Since the last general elections, we’ve won fantastically all elections in which we have contested. There’s a reason for that. It’s because we prepare. We do our homework.

“Nigerians bought in and voted for our party massively in 2023. We won that election, even though there are elements who want to claim that they won without evidence. But we won that election without question. As I said a few minutes ago, in every other

election that has been called since then, Nigerians voted, not Indians. Nigerians voted in all the other elections since 2023. We won by upwards of 90 per cent.

“Let me remind you that the APC is the governing party in this country, put in office by Nigerians. Already, the answer to your question has been codified in an election in which the APC is governing, not just at the centre, but in so many states in our country.”

On the APC’s chances in 2027, he said: “We will win the election. We are working hard to win the election. I think that Nigerians are going to stand tall, shoulder to shoulder with the APC to win the next election.”

World.title: Peter Mbah and the Road to Awhum
World.content:
By Olusegun Adeniyi

On Monday morning, I received two videos that left me thinking about the state of leadership in our country. The first came from a local government area in one of the Northeast states. The council chairman had reportedly died, and his deputy was being sworn in to complete the tenure. What should have been a routine constitutional exercise turned into an uncomfortable spectacle. Here was a man about to assume responsibility for an entire local government, yet he appeared unable to repeat the words of the oath being administered to him. It was an awkward moment, but the more important question was not how the man performed before the camera; it was how he emerged as the person expected to inherit such a critical leadership position in the first place. The second video came from the South-east. It showed the deplorable condition of the road leading to Awhum Waterfall in Enugu State, a natural attraction whose beauty ought to make it a source of pride for the community and our country.

I decided to forward the two videos directly to the governors of the respective states. I do that quite often based on my conviction that to whom you can whisper, you don’t always need to shout. Only one of the two governors responded: Peter Mbah of Enugu State. I will not name the other governor who had not responded as at the time of sending in this column last night. The point is not to embarrass or turn a private exchange into a contest between political officeholders. It is to examine what these encounters tell us about leadership.

To be fair, governors receive enormous volumes of messages, and no reasonable person should expect them to personally respond to everyone. It is also possible that the other governor acted on the information without replying to me. He could also have decided that he was helpless about the situation depicted in the video. But the question remains: in a political culture where citizens often struggle to get the attention of those who govern them, what should we make of a leader who responds when a problem is brought to his attention? Mbah called me about two hours after receiving the video message. He said he agreed with the complainants. “You cannot talk about tourism with a road like that so they are quite correct,” Mbah said. “But what they do not know is that the road will soon be constructed. You can see that it has been cleared.”

In public service, accountability begins with acknowledging a problem and indicating that something was being done about it. But let me also add a qualification. A response is not a completed road, and a promise is not a project delivered. To that extent, Mbah’s assurance must be tested against what happens on the ground. Nevertheless, there is value in his willingness to engage with information that may help government do its job. The larger issue here is that public officials must remain ever attentive to issues of concern to the ordinary people. From Abuja to many of the 36 states, we don’t often see that. In recent months, Nigerians have been groaning under the yoke of skyrocketing prices of goods and services that are priced beyond them. It doesn’t appear as if anybody is listening.

On Monday, the 2026 Global Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) report by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) confirmed the level of deprivation in our country: an additional 17.9 million Nigerians slipped into poverty between 2021 and 2024. Meanwhile, only God knows how many more millions may have slipped even further in the last two years. With the multidimensional poverty rate increasing to 38.7 percent in 2024 from 33 percent in 2021, Nigeria recorded the largest increase among the five countries that experienced a rise over their latest measurement periods. We performed even worse than Afghanistan, the Central African Republic, Guinea and Kyrgyzstan! Amid all these, the only response we have received from the federal government is a meaningless 30-day ‘fuel discount’ from the NNPC that appears more like an attempt to trivialize a serious problem.

To worsen matters, we have become too familiar with the futility of voice. And the government, especially this government, seems to capitalize on that to take Nigerians for granted. Yet, in a functioning democracy, citizens must have reason to believe that speaking up is worthwhile because when the ordinary channels for expressing dissatisfaction repeatedly fail, disillusionment accumulates. And when that happens for a long time, there are usually consequences. So, in the context of this intervention, a message to a governor is not only a modest form of civic engagement, but also an opportunity to see whether the connection between citizens and the state is still functioning.

Now, the two videos raise different questions, and it is important not to confuse them. Let me begin with the Northeast video. On 11 July 2024, the Supreme Court delivered its landmark judgment on local government financial autonomy, directing that allocations from the Federation Account be paid directly to each of the 774 local government areas in the country and rejecting the use of caretaker committees in place of democratically elected councils. The judgment addressed a longstanding distortion in our federal arrangement: the control exercised by governors over institutions constitutionally recognised as the third tier of government.

The reasoning behind local government autonomy is compelling. Local governments are closest to the people, and resources intended for grassroots development should serve that purpose. But financial autonomy, important as it is, cannot by itself guarantee good governance. The quality of the leaders entrusted with those resources matters just as much. This is where our local government elections deserve closer scrutiny. I have written on this many times, including Democracy and the Grassroots – THISDAYLIVE. When the political process offers little meaningful competition, accountability can begin to flow upwards to the governor and the party structure, not downwards to the people who should be the ultimate beneficiaries of local government.

In such circumstances, the question of who becomes a council chairman or deputy chairman risks being settled within the political machinery as against a serious assessment of the candidate’s preparedness for public service. That is a problem because a deputy is not an ornament on an electoral ticket. The office exists partly to provide continuity when the principal can no longer serve. A deputy governor, vice-president or vice-chairman may be called upon to assume the responsibilities of leadership at a moment of crisis. The person must therefore be prepared for that eventuality. The lesson is not that every transition will be seamless or that the ability to recite an oath is a complete measure of competence. It is that institutions must be prepared to function when circumstances demand it. The death of an officeholder is never something an institution can schedule, but it must be prepared for the possibility.

I take no pleasure in the video from the Northeast. Nerves can betray anyone, and fluency in English is not a reliable measure of intelligence, integrity, or the ability to serve a community. Some of our most effective grassroots leaders communicate far more comfortably in their indigenous languages. It would therefore be unfair to reduce a person’s entire capacity for leadership to an awkward moment before a camera. But the video should prompt a more serious question: what process produced this man as the person next in line, and what had been done to prepare him for the responsibilities of that office? That is a question for the political party, the electoral system and the institutions concerned. It is not an invitation to ridicule an individual.

Now to Awhum. In the video, approximately five motorbikers shared their terrible experience on the road. “The natural wonders need more than admiration; they need proper care and investment,” they said while adding that the story of Awhun is similar to that of other neglected tourism sites in Nigeria. As an aside, the late Chief Ojo Maduekwe–who served as Minister of Culture and Tourism between 1999 and 2000 under President Olusegun Obasanjo–once told me a story of an experience shared with him by a group of foreign tourists traveling across West Africa. On arriving Seme border, they were asked for their purpose of seeking to enter Nigeria and the visitors told the border control and immigration officers that they were tourists. “Please tell us your real reason. This is not Kenya. There is nothing like tourism in Nigeria,” the visitors were reportedly told. In a way, those border control officials sounded truer than they probably intended!

The potential for tourism in Nigeria is huge because there is an abundance of natural attractions across the country. Each of these natural attractions, properly developed, can sustain a local economy by creating opportunities for tour guides, transport operators, accommodation providers, food vendors and other small businesses. But tourism is an ecosystem. A waterfall does not become an economic asset simply because it is beautiful or because a government includes it in a brochure. Visitors need accessible roads, adequate facilities, safety, sanitation and reliable information. The people who live around the attraction must also have a stake in whatever economic activity it generates.

Enugu State has announced ambitious tourism plans. In May 2025, the state government unveiled a tourism development programme reportedly valued at about N30 billion, with N13.8 billion approved for the first phase. Awhum was among the attractions identified for development, including proposals for a canopy walkway and boardwalk. In July 2026, the State Executive Council reportedly approved an Okpatu–Awhum cable car project. These are significant ambitions but the test of a tourism programme is not the number of projects announced. It is whether the investments make the destination more accessible, improve the experience of visitors and create lasting value for the surrounding community.

A cable car may become an attraction in its own right, but visitors will still need to travel to the area. Residents, traders and service providers will depend on the road as part of the everyday infrastructure of a living community. If the road is improved, the people will experience the difference. If it remains in its present condition, the governor’s response will count for little beyond the courtesy of acknowledging a message. Therefore, while Mbah may have demonstrated a willingness to engage, the verdict remains open. The road to Awhum will provide part of the answer. The ball is now squarely in his court. I am aware that Mbah has delivered on many promises in Enugu State. I hope he also delivers on the construction of a proper road to Awhum.

On Anthony Kila

In a column last year titled, Parade of ‘Oluwole’ Certificates – THISDAYLIVE, I wrote about how many of our sacrosanct institutions in Nigeria have been invaded by a national culture of fraud: “In religion, charlatans have crowned themselves Pastors, Bishops, Imams, General Overseers etc. In the hospitals, patients are at the mercy of fake doctors and pharmacists whose prescriptions are often fatal. In the construction industry, quacks have taken over, causing buildings to collapse after mere drizzle. In academia, there is an epidemic of ‘professors’ who disseminate ignorance to unsuspecting students.”

Despite the foregoing, I must confess being shocked by the revelations about the academic credentials being paraded by Mr Anthony Kila. Although I have never had the opportunity of a personal interaction with him, Kila is someone I admired from distance based on his public engagements. On Tuesday, I saw a post on an X handle, @DailyJusticeAct, which summed up the unfortunate saga for me: “Kila’s fall is not merely shocking it is quietly devastating. For years, his calm voice, measured eloquence and careful articulation lent weight to every argument. Many of us leaned in, persuaded not only by what he said but by the quiet authority with which he said it. Now the allegations of forged credentials, stretched across degrees, titles, and institutions, leave that trust fractured. His performance was compelling but the foundation, if the reports hold, was not. Deception of this scale is never just personal it is a public wound.”

As I stated in the column under reference, forging academic credentials are mere symptoms of the crisis of values that bedevil our country today. But it is nonetheless very depressing when someone you hold in high esteem turns out to be no more than an imposter.

A Tragic Sisters’ Act

In his work on human behaviour and resilience, Dr. Alex Lickerman, a former assistant professor of Medicine at the University of Chicago, referenced the tragic case involving a six-year-old girl named Jacqueline Johnson who stepped in front of a moving train after leaving a suicide note saying that she “wanted to be with her mother” who had just died from a terminal illness. “This is the power of the human mind,” Lickerman wrote. “A girl in kindergarten thinks of the past and imagines a future that is so bleak, so devoid of meaningful moments without her mom, that she takes her own life,”

There is a way in which that tragedy resembles that of three British sisters of Nigerian descent (Jane Adetoro, 36, Christina Walters, 32, and Rebecca Walters, 31) who in May this year drowned in the sea off Brighton, United Kingdom. Last Thursday, a coronal inquest into their deaths revealed that in the days before the tragedy, the sisters made a trip together to Birmingham to visit the former home of their mother, Janice Adetoro, who died by drowning in 2010. In the postmortem conducted after their bodies were found, there was no evidence of drugs or alcohol or that they had been subjected to violence, according to the inquest. But references to water and suicide were found on the laptop of one of them. Penelope Schofield told the court: “These three sisters lived very secluded lives; they were incredibly private. We don’t know why they took this course of action…It is not for the court to speculate and sadly these reasons may never be known.”

Since some wounds are invisible to the eye, we can only rely on the wisdom of David O. McKay that “the most important of life’s battles is the one we fight daily in the silent chambers of the soul.” The distraught father of the ladies, Joseph Jacobson, said in a written statement: “There are no words that can adequately express the pain of losing a child. To lose all three of my precious daughters, Jane, Christina and Rebecca, is a heartbreak beyond anything I could ever have imagined.”

May God continue to comfort him and other members of the family.

World.title: Expert Explores Fossil Energy, Sustainability Puzzle at PAU
World.content:
Pan-Atlantic University (PAU) hosted its 26th inaugural lecture, delivered by Professor Ekundayo Peter Mesagan, Professor of Energy and Environmental Economics in the School of Management and Social Sciences (SMSS), at the Honeywell Group Auditorium, Lagos Business School.

At the inaugural lecturer, the PAU Vice-Chancellor, Professor Enase Okonedo, described Professor Mesagan as “an economist, researcher and policy advisor whose work spans energy and environmental economics, industrial policy, natural resources and sustainable economic development.”

Delivering the lecture titled: ‘Making Lemonade from Lemons: The Fossil Energy & Sustainability Puzzle’, Mesagan examined the tension between the global push for environmental sustainability and the developmental realities of oil-rich and energy-deficient nations. He framed the discussion with a central question: “In the last few decades, the global argument for environmental sustainability has been that we should deemphasise the use of fossil energy while scaling up other forms of energy that are less carbon-dioxide emitting. Is this true or not? What should happen to oil-rich nations, especially developing countries? Should they fold up, or should they seek alternative sources of income for financing their projects?”

He argued that the energy transition is far more complex than simply substituting fossil fuels with renewables, as technological and cost constraints mean fossil fuels will remain part of the global energy mix for the foreseeable future.

World.title: Foundation Signs MoU on Mentorship of 100 Tech Scholarship
World.content:
The Leo Stan Ekeh Foundation (LSEF) has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Nigeria Computer Society (NCS) to provide mentorship, technical training and real-world technology experience to the Nigerian whizkids under the Foundation’s technology scholarship initiative.

The 1000 scholarship scheme, which was first announced by the Chairman of Zinox Group, Leo Stan Ekeh, is designed to empower indigent but exceptionally gifted Nigerian students to study Computer Science and other technology-related disciplines in federal and state universities, as well as polytechnics, across the country.

According to the Director of LSEF, Dr. George Emetuche, the programme will feature boot camps each semester, creating opportunities for students to learn beyond the classroom and gain practical experience. The objective, he explained, would be to prepare beneficiaries not merely to graduate, but to become capable technology professionals who can solve real-world problems.

Speaking at the ceremony, NCS President, Professor Muhammed Siraju Aliyu, described Leo Stan Ekeh as a nationalist who has consistently supported initiatives that create opportunities for Nigerians who may otherwise lack access.

He noted that Ekeh’s relationship with the NCS predates the scholarship initiative and has contributed to the advancement of technology and human capital development.

Representing the Zinox Group, Executive Director, Human Resources, Mrs. Chioma Nwoke, assured the foundation and the NCS of the group’s continued support for the initiative, cohort after cohort.

World.title: NCC, Others to Address Internet Peering, Improve Traffic
World.content:
Network Operators Group (ngNOG), in collaboration with the Internet Exchange Point of Nigeria (IXPN) and the Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC), is set to hold the 2026 Nigerian Peering and Interconnect Forum (ngPIF), that will focus on strengthening internet peering and interconnection, as well as improving local traffic exchange.

The two-day forum, scheduled to hold in Lagos will also focus on building the infrastructure needed to support Nigeria’s rapidly expanding digital economy.

According to the organisers, Nigeria’s internet infrastructure is at a critical stage, a development that has prompted regulators, network operators, Internet Service Providers (ISPs), Data Centre operators and technology companies to converge at the 2026 Nigerian Peering and Interconnect Forum, to tackle local traffic, interconnection and the future of Nigeria’s digital infrastructure.

The convenor of ngNOG, Prof. Adewale Adedokun, said the forum became necessary at a time when Nigeria must take a more strategic approach to how internet traffic is exchanged, content is delivered and digital services are hosted.

World.title: Firm Wins Digital Payments Platform of the Year Award
World.content:
PalmPay, has been named Digital Payments Platform of the Year at the 2026 BusinessDay Banks and Other Financial Institutions (BAFI) Awards, recognising the company’s contribution to the growth of digital payments and financial inclusion in Nigeria.

The BAFI Awards organised by BusinessDay and held in Lagos, was officially presented to PalmPay by the publisher and co-founder of BusinessDay, Mr. Frank Aigbogun.

Since launching in Nigeria in 2019, PalmPay has built an inclusive digital financial services ecosystem, enabling customers to make payments, pay bills, and access other financial services through its platform. The company now serves over 35 million users in Nigeria, supported by a broad network of merchants and agents that enables digital transactions across the country.

Commenting on the recognition, Managing Director, PalmPay Nigeria, Chika Nwosu, said the award reflected the company’s commitment to building financial services around the everyday needs of Nigerians.

“We are honoured to receive the Digital Payments Platform of the Year award at the BAFI Awards. Digital payments have become an important part of how Nigerians manage their finances, run businesses and carry out everyday transactions. This award reflects our continued commitment to making financial services more accessible, reliable and secure for the millions of customers who use PalmPay every day,” Nwosu said.

World.title: TikTok Moves to Resolve Access Restriction in Northern Nigeria
World.content:
Worried about the continued restriction and disruption to TikTok access in some parts of northern Nigeria, TikTok has explained that it did not implement any restriction order on its platform in some parts of northern Nigeria, and has assured its customers of its resolve to address the issue.

TikTok spokesperson gave the clarification in a statement, where he said: “We are aware of reports regarding restricted access to our platform in certain parts of Nigeria. We can confirm that this restriction was not implemented by TikTok. We are actively engaging with relevant stakeholders to resolve the situation and remain committed to ensuring access for our community.”

This is coming just as the Coalition of Civil Society Organisations has called on the federal government to carry out a prompt, transparent and independent investigation on the recent disruption to TikTok access in some parts of northern Nigeria.

The coalition urged government and regulators to prioritise transparency, accountability, technical verification and respect for freedom of expression and access to information, while ensuring that any legitimate concerns relating to security, public order or unlawful online activity are addressed through targeted, lawful and proportionate measures rather than unexplained disruption of access to an entire communications platform.

World.title: Report: African Cities Rank among Global AI Adopters Despite Infrastructure Deficits
World.content:
Emma Okonji

Global cities like London, Dubai, New York City, Washington DC, and Amsterdam top the rankings of the world’s most intelligent cities according to new research from Boston Consulting Group (BCG).

Although listed cities excel in different areas, none of them is leading across every domain, underscoring that no city has mastered every relevant dimension.

The report also revealed an interesting urban trend across Africa’s major economic hubs, citing African cities like Lagos in Nigeria, Johannesburg in South Africa, Casablanca in Morocco, and Cairo in Egypt, as African cities that are high adopters of Artificial Intelligence (AI) technology globally, despite infrastructure deficits.

While all four cities currently sit in the report’s “Developing” maturity tier due to deficits in digital infrastructure and star-tup funding, the citizens of the listed African cities are among the most active and optimistic AI adopters globally, the report said.

The report, tagged: “BCG’s Intelligent Cities Index 2026: How AI Shapes Urban Living’, is the firm’s inaugural assessment of how 61 of the world’s biggest cities across 39 countries use technology to serve their residents and businesses. The report evaluated cities across five domains of intelligent city maturity: outcomes, strategy, adoption, ways of working, and enablers. The report is of the view that a city’s overall maturity level reflects its combined maturity across domains such as leading, accelerating, emerging, or developing.”

Addressing African’s lead in citizen’s AI appetite, the report viewed the African indices as supercharged by young demographics, where over 50 per cent of the population in Cairo, Casablanca, and Lagos is under the age of 35, as these cities land squarely in the “AI Enthusiasts” cohort.

According to the report, Casablanca achieved a top ranking in AI adoption and smart city app usage, outpacing numerous established international metropolises.

The report also found that cities do not need to begin with or focus solely on world-class infrastructure or deep funding ecosystems to improve resident outcomes. “Expanding intelligent AI-enabled city services can strengthen quality of life and overall intelligent city maturity regardless of a city’s starting point, demonstrating that multiple pathways exist to becoming a smarter city, aligned with each city’s current maturity across domains, “the report said.

The report uncovered a clear alignment between how frequently residents use Generative AI (GenAI) tools and how positively they view AI’s future impact.

According to the report, residents who use AI most often are also the most optimistic about the technology’s potential to improve opportunity, productivity, and quality of life.

“This creates a virtuous circle. Positive experiences with AI increase resident confidence, giving city leaders a further opening to enable AI more fully and provide more value to beneficiaries through new and improved intelligent city services. This value feeds yet more optimism, which drives more engagement, innovation, and scaling as the cycle repeats,” the report said, adding that cities in Africa, Asia, and the Middle East are particularly prominent in this pattern, showing the strongest GenAI momentum, pairing high usage with high optimism about its future impact.

Analysing the report, the Managing Director and Partner at BCG, Akram Awad, who is also the co-author of the report, said: “AI is a key foundation of the intelligent city, and AI adoption and optimism are not confined to the ‘usual suspects’ technology hubs. Cities around the world are creating value for residents in different ways and from different starting points. We built the Intelligent Cities Index to provide an objective, holistic view of how cities shape and enable their AI ambitions and how effectively those ambitions translate into meaningful improvements in people’s lives.”

Partner and Director at BCG, Rami Mourtada, who is also a co-author of the report said: “Given today’s rapid pace of change and evolving resident expectations, building a city’s intelligent foundation, paired with focused improvement across enablers requires urgency. But city leaders and business partners don’t need to try to do everything all at once. It’s a longer-term horizon and there is no single pathway forward. Intelligent city momentum comes from making intentional, and sometimes incremental, choices now and building for a smarter tomorrow with a clear, comprehensive roadmap.”

To move from “Developing” to higher maturity tiers, the report emphasises that African city leaders must address critical “soft enabler” bottlenecks; specifically venture capital access, tech talent retention, and institutional AI governance.

However, BCG’s analysis showed that cities do not need world-class infrastructure to make progress.

“By adopting a “focused specialist” approach, African urban centres can partner with local innovation ecosystems to deploy targeted, incremental AI services that address residents’ most immediate daily needs, converting grassroots enthusiasm into long-term economic growth, “the report further said.

World.title: ITU, WMO Move to Protect Global Radio Spectrum for Weather, Climate and Water Services
World.content:
Emma Okonji

The International Telecommunication Union (ITU) and the World Meteorological Organisation (WMO), have called on governments, regulators, and meteorologists across globe, to safeguard access and interference to radio frequency spectrum essential for weather forecasts, early warnings, climate monitoring and water management.

The appeal came with the release of a new joint handbook, titled: ‘Use of Radio Spectrum for Meteorology: Weather, Climate, Water and Related Environmental Applications.’

The new publication by ITU and WMO, offered updated guidance on the use and protection of radio frequencies supporting critical meteorological systems. These systems enable observations of the atmosphere, oceans, and land, and the transmission of data that supports life-saving early warnings, reliable weather forecasting, and long-term climate monitoring.

The ITU-WMO handbook, formally released at the opening of the Global ITU-WMO Seminar on Spectrum Use for Meteorology, also highlighted the potential impact of radio-frequency interference on the accuracy and availability of essential environmental data.

Speaking on how best to protect radio spectrum from interference, Secretary-General of ITU, Doreen Bogdan-Martin, said: “Preventing harmful radio interference is a matter of public safety and can save lives. Interference-free spectrum keeps weather forecasts accurate, emergency alerts and warnings timely, and climate data reliable. With this, communities can prepare, respond and build resilience.”

WMO Secretary-General Celeste Saulo, said: “The radio-frequency spectrum is a finite natural resource. Meteorology relies on specific bands — determined not by choice, but by the physical properties of the atmosphere itself: they enable observations that no other frequencies can provide. These bands must be protected. Protect the spectrum that lets us observe the atmosphere, and we protect forecasts and early warnings on which every country depends.”

In Nigeria, the Nigerian Meteorological Agency (NiMet), has made several forecasts on weather across regions, with warnings on possible flood in some parts of Nigeria. NiMet’s prediction and warning stems from the update it gets from the radio spectrum band assigned to Nigeria by the ITU, which it seeks to protect globally.

For instance, NiMet recently predicted a mix of three-day rainfall, sunshine and thunderstorms across Nigeria from Monday October 12 to Wednesday October 14, 2026. The agency envisaged thunderstorms accompanied by moderate rainfall over parts of Ondo, Osun, Ogun, Lagos, Imo Abia, Enugu, Ebonyi, Anambra, Cross River, Akwa Ibom, Rivers, Bayelsa, Edo and Delta states, and warned that strong winds could precede thunderstorms in affected areas and urged residents to secure loose objects to prevent accidents.

According to ITU, some satellite sensors measure very weak naturally occurring signals at specific frequencies, making protection from harmful interference particularly important.

“Weather radar, lightning location systems, aircraft and marine observations, hydrological monitoring systems, and other platforms also rely on these frequency bands to collect and exchange data, “Bogdan-Martin said.

In order to protect critical global resource like radio spectrum, ITU said experts at the forthcoming WMO-ITU event would review recent and upcoming international spectrum decisions relevant to meteorological and earth observation services, including outcomes of the latest ITU World Radiocommunication Conferences.

The ITU World Radiocommunication Conferences came as the demand for wireless communications, satellite services, and environmental data continues to grow, underscoring the importance of ensuring continued access to, and protection of radio-frequency spectrum for earth observation.

“Radio frequency interference can degrade the accuracy and availability of vital data needed for early warning systems, weather forecasting, and climate monitoring. Such impacts can affect the ability of governments and communities to prepare for and respond to environmental hazards.

“Bringing technical, operational, and regulatory guidance together in one resource, the new handbook supports informed decision-making on spectrum management and promotes collaboration between the meteorological and radiocommunication communities, “ITU said in a statement.

World.title: ‘Uyena’: Social media reacts to Nathi Mthethwa’s lookalike [photos]
Rachel Kolisi shows up for Siya’s Stormers homecoming [video]
World.content:
Rachel Kolisi watched the Stormers match, and her ex Siya Kolisi, over the weekend. Images via IG

Rachel Kolisi has been hailed a “super mom” after taking her children and their friends to watch her ex, Siya Kolisi’s Stormers homecoming match last weekend.

The mom-of-two and her rugby-player ex announced their marriage split two years ago. While Siya has moved on with a woman named Rachel John, his former spouse has remained single.

The 35-year-old has returned to the Cape Town club in a bid to be closer to his family.



RACHEL KOLISI SUPPORTS SIYA’S STORMERS HOMECOMING

On her TikTok account, Rachel Kolisi vlogged a “day in the life” video about her busy weekend

This included hosting a dozen children for her son Nick’s 12th birthday celebrations and taking the kids to watch the Stormers match against the Sharks at the DHL Stadium .

In the video, Rachel dons a Stormers rugby shirt while cheering from the stands.

She zooms onto the pitch, seemingly at her ex, Siya Kolisi, who celebrated his homecoming match.

Rachel says in the vlog: “I haven’t been to a live game in ages, so it was super fun. The kids had a great time”.

@rachelkolisi A little bit of everything, all in a day 🤍  ♬ original sound – Rachel Kolisi

HAPPY TO BE HOME

Like his ex, Rachel Kolisi, Siya Kolisi appears happy to be home after his return to Cape Town and the Stormers.

The 35-year-old has been enjoying the sights and cuisine of the Western Province in his social media posts.

World.title: Angelique Gerber to DIVORCE ex-Bok Jacques Potgieter
World.content:
Angelique Gerber will reportedly proceed with her divorce to former Springbok, Jacques Potgieter, four years after their marriage separation.

This comes as the ex 7de Laan actress reportedly had a brief reconciliation with her ex, who is the father of her three children.

During the time apart, Jacques had a relationship with another woman, whom he recently split from.



ANGELIQUE GERBER TO DIVORCE EX JACQUES POTGIETER

According to reports, Angelique Gerber is proceeding with her divorce from Jacques Potgieter after allegedly giving him a second chance.

Sadly, their recent reconciliation was short-lived, with Angelique’s lawyer confirming that the second split was in the best interests of their three children.

The actress and influencer reportedly had enough of Jacques’s lifestyle and is now ready to close the chapter.

The news that Jacques and Angelique are still legally married, despite their messy relationship split, came as a surprise to many followers.

On her social media platforms, Jacques had liked comments urging the couple to rekindle their romance. When one follower commented, “You know you two can marry again”, Jacques responded, “We were never divorced”.

TIMELINE OF MESSY MARRIAGE SPLIT

Take a look at this relationship timeline between Angelique Gerber and Jacques Potgieter…



2014: Angelique and Jacques begin dating. At the time, the red-haired actress appeared as the character “Clara” on SABC 2 soapie, 7de Laan, which her rugby player boyfriend played for both the Waratahs and the Munakata Sanix Blues

2016: Angelique and Jacqued married at a Durbanville estate.

2016-2018: The couple would welcome their three children.

2021: Jacques Potgieter denies posting several Instagram Stories confessing to cheating on his wife, Angelique. He claims his account was “hacked”. On her IG, Angelique posted the cryptic message “The truth always comes out”. The couple again deny posting the messages. They claim they are happier and more in love than ever.

2022: The couple appeared in public separately and deleted all images of themselves together. Jacques goes public with a woman named Lizane “Lalla” Wagner.

2023: Angelique Gerber puts Jacques Potgieter on blast over a dispute over financial support for their children. She also expressed her annoyance at his posts praising his girlfriend as a stepmother.

June 2026: Jacques and Lizane Wagner split after their four-year relationship. Lizane denied allegations that she had been responsible for the breakdown of Jacques’s marriage.

July – September 2026: Jacques and Angelique appear to rekindle their romance. Jacques likes comments from the public encouraging the couple to give their marriage a “second chance”

October 2026: Jacques deletes all of his new images with Angelique, who also allegedly accuses him of “betraying” his family in various cryptic IG reposts.

World.title: ‘The R2 400 is just an insult’: Pensioner speaks out on SASSA grant
World.content:
A pensioner in Limpopo who receives the Older Person’s Grant says his monthly SASSA payment does not cover his household’s basic needs.

The grant recipient, who asked not to be named in this article, has received the grant for three years. He lives in a shared family home where three to five people depend on his income, and he uses his grant for a mix of essential expenses.

Despite this, he regularly struggles to make ends meet. He runs out of money before the month ends.



SASSA grant falls short for pensioner

The pensioner said the cost of living and rising food prices are his biggest financial concern. When asked what he would change about SASSA, he chose an increase in the grant amount.

“SASSA must stop harassing and stopping us when we try to find other income streams because the R2 400 is just an insult, period,” he said.

The Older Person’s Grant increased by R80 to R2 400 per month in April 2026, following Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana’s Budget Speech.

The grant recipient has experience in administrative and office work. He is currently unemployed and not looking for work.

Payment problems and poor communication

The pensioner said he has experienced a late or missing grant payment. He rated SASSA’s communication with recipients as very poor.

He receives his grant through a bank deposit. He has never applied for additional government support because he did not know what else was available.

If you receive a SASSA grant and want to share your story, we want to hear from you.

Take part in our survey and stand a chance to win R2 000. Your responses help us tell the stories that matter.

World.title: ‘A star is needed here in Naturena’: Moloisane on Kaizer Chiefs’ trophy target
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs defender Thabo Moloisane has set his sights on winning trophies and helping Amakhosi end their long wait for league glory following his arrival at Naturena in July.

The 26-year-old was one of five new signings brought in ahead of the season and has already featured in the majority of the club’s matches.

Speaking ahead of Chiefs’ clash against Stellenbosch FC on Tuesday, Moloisane made it clear that winning silverware is a major priority in his first season with the Soweto giants.



The defender believes Amakhosi have an opportunity to challenge for the league title and is determined to play his part in ending the club’s lengthy wait for another Premiership crown.

“A star, guys, it is needed here at home. We have an opportunity to see if we can do it this season, and the league, of course. It is one thing that has gone past us for a long time and, for me, in my first season, I just want to get as many trophies as I can. That’s where the ambition is, and the rest can follow,” he said.

Kaizer Chiefs last won the league title in the 2014/15 season, and Moloisane is eager to help restore the club’s status as one of South African football’s leading forces.



Beyond his ambitions at club level, the defender is also hoping to work his way back into the Bafana Bafana setup.

Kaizer Chiefs star wants Bafana return

Moloisane acknowledged that returning to the national team will not be easy, given the competition for places, but believes hard work and consistent performances at a high-profile club like Kaizer Chiefs could improve his chances.

“We should give credit to the guys, you know. I was speaking to Mdu (Shabalala) last week, saying the line is long to get back into Bafana, but at the same time, I’m at a big institution watched by everyone. For me, it’s just to continue working hard. The journey is still long,” he told media.



For Moloisane, the immediate focus remains on delivering for Amakhosi and helping the club compete for honours, while keeping his hopes of a Bafana Bafana recall alive.

Will he win a star?

World.title: ‘Spirit of lust’: Bernard Parker hints at struggles?
World.content:
Bernard Parker has reposted several telling Instagram posts, hinting at infidelity, lust and a “miserable marriage”. This comes as the former Bafana and Kaizer Chiefs player – now coach of TS Galaxy – announced his split from his baby mama, Kacha Stepanovic, in a social media post.

The 40-year-old has not disclosed when or why he separated from his wife, Wendy Parker, whom he married in 2012.

BERNARD PARKER’S CRYPTIC REPOSTS

On his Instagram account, Bernard Parker has reposted several telling faith-based Reels about men who seemingly struggle with monogamy.



One was about “the spirit of lust” and featured a preacher warning Christians about “sex with demons”. Others were warnings about lust and “staying away from bad women”

Another was a segment of a message from a preacher, which was titled: “What to do when your marriage is miserable”. A different message featured another preacher calling on individuals to ask their families and partners for forgiveness after “destroying” a marriage.

‘PERSONAL ADDICTIONS’

In his statement posted on Monday, 12 October, Bernard Parker alluded to being unfaithful to his former partner, Kacha Stepanovic, who is allegedly the mother of his baby daughter.

He shared: “I want to be honest about my part in our journey. I have made mistakes and struggled with personal addictions that have affected my life and the people I love.

“Kacha, I’m truly sorry for the times I hurt you, let you down, and caused you pain. You gave me love, support, patience and kindness that I’ve never received before. I take responsibility for my mistakes, knowing that some things cannot simply be undone with an apology”

On her social media account, Kacha Stepanovic reposted Bernard Parker’s statement.



She also hinted at his alleged infidelity.

She shared on her IG Stories: “Lust and addiction will strip you of your family, your work, your name and everything you built.

“If betrayal was so easy, the devil would be next seated at the throne. Make sure whatever you do is worth losing it all”.

World.title: South Africa will host race by 2029 - McKenzie
World.content:
PRETORIA - Sports Minister Gayton McKenzie insists South Africa did not miss out on hosting Formula 1.

Despite Rwanda getting the rights to host the African Grand Prix in the 2030s, McKenzie remains upbeat that the country is still on track to host the event in the near future.

He was addressing the media in Pretoria on Wednesday.

World.title: State claims Sibiya's lawyers interfered with witnesses
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The legal team for former Deputy National Police Commissioner Shadrack Sibiya has wrapped up its bail argument.



Sibiya's lawyer, Estelle Killian, has argued that he is not a flight risk or a threat to witnesses, emphasising that they have not interfered with the complainants.



She urged the court to grant Sibiya bail because his health was at risk.



The State has opposed bail for Sibiya, accusing his defence team of attempting to secure a statement from a witness.



Prosecutors argued that this alleged interference provides plausible grounds for the court to deny his release.



eNCA reporter Pule Letshwiti-Jones has more details in the video above.

World.title: AKA's photographer testifies at murder trial
World.content:
DURBAN - The murder trial of rapper AKA and his friend, Tebello 'Tibz' Motsoane, has been adjourned until Thursday in the Durban High Court.



Four witnesses testified on Tuesday, including AKA’s manager and a DJ who was with them on the night of the murders.



On Wednesday, AKA’s photographer Thotloetso Mogotsi took the stand.



eNCA senior reporter Dasen Thathiah was at court and filed this report in the video above.

World.title: Three CIT robbery suspects shot and killed in KZN
World.content:
UMLAZI - Three suspected cash-in-transit robbers have been killed in a shootout with police and private security in Umlazi, KZN.

Initially, police had reported that four suspects were shot and killed, however, this number has since been revised to three by KwaZulu-Natal police spokesperson Robert Netshiunda.

Netshiunda said a manhunt for other suspects involved in this alleged robbery has been launched.

"We know with experience that there are getaway vehicles and there are those who were not at the crime scene. So, we don't know how many of them were at the crime scene, but a manhunt is on for those that we saw, which we are pursuing now," Netshiunda said.

He said four firearms were found at the scene and in one abandoned vehicle, officials found cash believed to be that which was stolen.

World.title: CheckPoint Podcast | Is South Africa's Middle Class Paying Twice To Survive? Xhanti Payi | 14 October 2026
World.content:
The Hidden Cost Of Paying Privately For Public Services In South Africa

A household can afford to pay its taxes and still find itself buying essential services all over again. The wider consequences reach beyond family budgets.

A salary increase should, in theory, leave a household with more room to breathe. There might be money available to save, improve a home, take a holiday or invest in

a small business. But for many South Africans, additional income does not necessarily translate into greater financial freedom. It may simply create an opportunity to purchase privately what the public system has failed to provide reliably.

Consider the decisions facing a household that relies on a salary to meet its obligations. Parents may pay school fees because they believe a particular school offers their children better opportunities. A family might maintain medical cover for greater certainty about access to healthcare. Private security, backup electricity and dependable internet connectivity can all become regular expenses. These choices differ across households, and public provision is not uniformly inadequate. Yet the underlying question remains: how much income is left for building financial security once essential needs have been met?

This is the often-overlooked cost of unreliable public provision. Citizens contribute through taxation, but some also spend additional money securing alternatives. The result is not necessarily literal double billing for an identical service. It is a second layer of expenditure that can reduce disposable income and leave families more vulnerable when unexpected costs arise.

The issue becomes particularly revealing when transport is considered. A private vehicle is frequently discussed as a lifestyle purchase, but for some workers it is also a practical response to the limited availability, convenience or reliability of alternative transport. Owning a vehicle can offer independence, yet it comes with financing costs, fuel, maintenance and insurance. A household may therefore be spending heavily just to maintain reliable access to work.

Official statistics illustrate how significant transport already is. Statistics South Africa's Income and Expenditure Survey for 2022/23 found that transport accounted for 15.3% of household consumption expenditure, making it the third-largest spending category. The National Household Travel Survey of 2020 also recorded substantial dependence on minibus taxis and long journeys for many public-transport users. These surveys cover different periods, but together they show why transport deserves attention as an economic issue rather than merely a commuting problem.

There is a further complication: the middle class cannot be defined only by a salary band. Two people earning similar incomes may have very different levels of financial security. One could have manageable housing costs and relatively few dependants. The other might support an extended family, service debt and pay privately for several essential services. Their earnings may look similar on paper, while their ability to save or absorb an emergency differs considerably.

Economist Xhanti Payi raises this wider problem in a CheckPoint: The Podcast conversation with Nkepile Mabuse, describing the middle class as an economic shock absorber. It is a useful metaphor because the pressures do not stop with the individual household. When people devote more income to maintaining basic stability, they have less available for other purchases, investment and supporting new enterprises.

This does not mean that every private alternative is evidence of government failure. Families make choices based on preferences, geography, convenience and affordability. Nor does it mean that public services can be improved simply by increasing expenditure. Reliability, management, maintenance and accountability matter as much as budget allocations.

The practical question for policymakers is what improvements would produce the greatest financial relief for households. A reliable transport system could lower commuting expenses. Better-maintained infrastructure could reduce the need for

private backup services. More dependable public institutions could make some household expenditure a matter of genuine choice rather than perceived necessity.

For households, the measure of economic progress cannot be salary growth alone. It must also include how much of that salary remains available after the essential costs of everyday life have been paid. A stronger middle class is not simply one that earns more. It is one that needs to spend less of its income compensating for systems that ought to work.

References:

· CheckPoint: The Podcast, 14 October 2026. Nkepile Mabuse in conversation with economist and strategist Xhanti Payi. Episode transcript.

· Statistics South Africa. *Transport Month: Key Data and Sector Insights* (2025), drawing on the Income and Expenditure Survey 2022/23.

· Statistics South Africa. *National Household Travel Survey 2020*, published 4 March 2021.

World.title: ‘They will not be forgotten’ - Boxer reacts to 3 employees gunned down at Eshowe.
World.content:
ESHOWE - Discount retailer Boxer has confirmed the deadly shooting of three of its employees at its Eshowe store in KwaZulu-Natal.

In a statement, Boxer said the employees were murdered on 10 October in what it called a ‘horrific act of violence’.

“Today, Boxer teams across the country observed a moment of remembrance before beginning their shifts, standing together in honour of our fallen colleagues,” the statement read in part.

CCTV footage of the incident has since circulated widely on social media.

The footage appears to show a man dressed in black clothing speaking to three employees inside an office before pulling out a gun and opening fire.

READ | Discount retailer Boxer announces profits and a new CEO

The three employees tried to take cover, but the alleged gunman continued to fire shots.

Details surrounding the circumstances that led to the incident were not disclosed in the statement; however, the retailer confirmed they are communicating with police.

“We are working closely with the SAPS and relevant authorities, providing our full cooperation and assistance with the ongoing investigation.”

The store has offered its condolences to employees' families.

World.title: Motorists, households face fresh fuel price hikes
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

EPRA attributed the price increases to the escalating conflict in the Middle East. [FIle, Standard]

The Energy and Petroleum Regulatory Authority (EPRA) has increased fuel prices, raising the cost of super petrol by Sh12.93 per litre, diesel by Sh9.90, and kerosene by Sh28.49.

The new prices, effective from October 15 to November 14, 2026, will see motorists in Nairobi pay up to Sh226.96 per litre for super petrol, Sh227.76 for diesel, and Sh219.85 for kerosene.

EPRA Director-General Edward Mwirigi Kinyua attributed the price increases to the escalating conflict in the Middle East, which has disrupted petroleum supply chains and driven up the cost of importing fuel.

The rise in kerosene prices is likely to hit low-income households that rely on the fuel for cooking and lighting.

Meanwhile, higher diesel prices could raise the cost of transporting goods and operating public service vehicles, potentially driving up fares and commodity prices.

Diesel is a key fuel for the country's freight transport sector and a significant portion of public service vehicle operations, meaning the increase could have a ripple effect across the economy.

The latest review comes after EPRA maintained pump prices during the September 15 to October 14 pricing period, despite a decline in the cost of importing petrol.

World.title: Oburu Oginga to leave hospital soon - ODM
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

ODM SG Catherine Omanyo criticised bloggers spreading unverified information about the veteran politician.

ODM Secretary General Catherine Omanyo has dismissed social media reports about the health of party leader Oburu Oginga, saying he is recovering well and is expected to be discharged from hospital either today or tomorrow.

Omanyo criticised bloggers spreading unverified information about the veteran politician, accusing them of exploiting his health condition to attract online attention and increase engagement.

“It's unfortunate what I've been reading on social media. Those people who are seeking to have more likes or viewers, they will be disappointed because he's up, he's well, he's fine. In fact, he's headed home either today or tomorrow,” she said.

Omanyo insisted that the reports had exaggerated his situation, dismissing claims of his death and assuring the public that he was doing well.

She noted that health conditions could fluctuate, saying Oburu's position as ODM party leader had made his well-being a subject of heightened public interest.

“Everybody, everybody, including you and me, our health is not static. You can be under the weather any time. It's just that he's a party leader, and it makes breaking news,” Omanyo said.

She urged social media users to exercise restraint when discussing the health of public figures, warning against spreading unverified reports, particularly claims of death, before confirmation from credible sources.

Her remarks come amid growing speculation on social media about Oburu's health, with some users circulating unverified claims about his condition.

World.title: Kenya declares Ebola a formidable epidemic disease, sets new rules
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale, who declared Ebola caused by the Bundibugyo virus a formidable epidemic disease under the Public Health Act. [File,Standard]

Kenya has declared Ebola virus a formidable epidemic disease, introducing new rules governing screening, isolation, quarantine, contact tracing and the handling of bodies.

Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale issued the declaration through a legal notice published in the Kenya Gazette on Monday, October 12, under Section 35 of the Public Health Act.

The declaration follows Kenya’s confirmation of its first imported case of Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease on October 6, after a Kenyan citizen who had been living in the Democratic Republic of Congo travelled through Uganda to Nairobi. The patient died despite receiving supportive treatment.

The case prompted health authorities to trace people who may have come into contact with the patient and strengthen screening at points of entry.

In an update on October 12, the World Health Organization (WHO) said Kenya had listed 127 contacts, with 94 in quarantine, and screened more than 665,000 travellers at points of entry.

WHO also supplied protective equipment and testing materials worth about US$70,000 to support the response.

The government published two legal notices on October 12. Legal Notice No. 203 declares the disease a formidable epidemic, while Legal Notice No. 204 establishes the Public Health (Ebola Disease) Rules, 2026.

The regulations provide for screening at points of entry, medical assessment, isolation, referral, quarantine and monitoring.

They also assign responsibilities to transport operators, health facilities, medical practitioners and laboratories.

Health authorities will conduct investigations and contact tracing, while designated health facilities will manage suspected and confirmed cases. The rules also provide for the inspection and decontamination of premises.

The regulations cover the safe and dignified disposal of bodies, burial procedures, record-keeping, transportation and repatriation. They also address public communication, media houses’ responsibilities in public sensitisation and assistance from enforcement agencies.

The rules provide for offences and penalties, although the Gazette extract does not specify the penalties for individual violations.

What the declaration means

Bundibugyo virus disease is a form of Ebola that spreads through direct contact with the blood or other bodily fluids of an infected person or contaminated materials.

Contact with the body of someone who has died from the disease can also expose people to infection during unsafe burial practices.

Symptoms can include fever, fatigue, muscle pain, headache and sore throat, followed by vomiting and diarrhoea. The incubation period ranges from two to 21 days.

WHO says no approved vaccine or specific treatment currently exists for the Bundibugyo strain, making early detection, isolation, supportive care and contact tracing central to controlling its spread.

The health agency has advised against travel or trade restrictions on Kenya, Uganda and the Democratic Republic of Congo based on the information available.

The new rules establish a legal framework for managing the disease, from identifying suspected infections and monitoring contacts to caring for patients and preventing exposure during burials.
